identity_held_roles.title: Sr Manager, Manufacturing - Electronics
identity_held_roles.description:
**About Advanced Energy**
Advanced Energy (Nasdaq: AEIS) is a global leader in the design and manufacturing of highly engineered, precision power conversion, measurement and control solutions for mission-critical applications and processes. AE’s power solutions enable customer innovation in complex applications for a wide range of industries including semiconductor equipment, industrial, manufacturing, telecommunications, data center computing and healthcare. Advanced Energy has devoted four decades to perfecting power for its global customers and is headquartered in Denver, Colorado.
 
 
Position Summary
 
 
The
**Senior Manager, Manufacturing**
is responsible for leading manufacturing operations across multiple AE locations, with a focus on
**complex electronic and electromechanical products and assemblies**
. This role ensures production efficiency, product quality, delivery performance, safety, and cost effectiveness while providing strategic and hands-on leadership to manufacturing supervisors and production teams.
 
 
Success in this role requires strong people leadership, strategic thinking, and significant practical experience in
**electronics, semiconductor, optics or high-tech manufacturing**
.
 
 
**Qualifications**
Required
 
 

* 8+ years of progressive experience in manufacturing operations, including at least 3 years in a manufacturing leadership role.
* Demonstrated manufacturing experience in electronics, electromechanical systems, semiconductor equipment, or other complex technical products.
* Practical knowledge of electronics manufacturing processes, such as PCB/PCBA assembly, electronic and electromechanical assembly, production testing, troubleshooting, inspection, and repair/rework.
* Experience managing manufacturing environments requiring disciplined process control, traceability, quality management, and configuration/change control.
* Demonstrated success applying Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, root-cause analysis, and structured continuous-improvement methods.
* Strong working knowledge of ERP/MRP systems and production-planning processes, including material requirements, capacity planning, scheduling, and inventory management.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop manufacturing supervisors and production teams.
* Experience partnering with Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Product/Program teams to resolve production issues and support new product introductions.
* Strong communication, analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills.
* Ability and willingness to travel domestically and internationally up to approximately 25%.
* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Operations, or a related field, or equivalent relevant experience.

**Preferred**

* Experience manufacturing high-mix, low-to-medium-volume electronic or electromechanical products.
* Experience with semiconductor capital equipment, precision electronics, power electronics, optical systems, or other technically complex equipment.
* Experience supporting new product introduction (NPI), design transfer, production ramp, and product lifecycle changes.
* Familiarity with IPC workmanship standards applicable to electronic assemblies.
* Experience with metrology, calibration, and inspection systems.
* Knowledge of applicable ISO quality-management standards and regulatory requirements.
* Experience leading manufacturing operations across multiple sites and/or internationally.
* Experience managing complex projects and cross-functional teams.

**COMPENSATION:**
*As required by multiple state pay transparency laws, Advanced Energy provides a reasonable range of compensation for each job posting. Actual compensation is influenced by an array of factors including, but not limited to, skill set, level of experience, and specific office location. The range of starting pay for this role is $150,000 to $190,000 per year.*
**BENEFITS:**
As part of our total rewards philosophy, we believe in offering and maintaining competitive compensation and benefits programs for our employees to attract and retain a talented, highly engaged workforce. Our compensation programs are focused on equitable, fair pay practices including market-based base pay, an annual pay-for-performance incentive plan for eligible positions, and a discounted Employee Stock Purchase Plan.
 
 
In addition to our competitive compensation practices, we offer a strong benefits package in each of the countries in which we operate. In the U.S., we offer a rich benefits package that includes:
 
 

* Medical - multiple medical plans are available to choose from
* Short and long-term disability and life insurance
* Health savings and flexible spending accounts
* Generous time off policy starting with 3 weeks of paid vacation, 7 days of paid sick time, and 12 paid holidays
* 8 hours of paid volunteer time off
* 8 weeks of paid parental leave for both Moms and Dads
* Company matched 401(k)
* Tuition reimbursement
* Expanded mental health coverage and employee assistance programs
* Other voluntary benefits include critical illness, accident and hospital indemnity, pet insurance, identify theft, and legal assistance

**Advanced Energy is committed to diversity in its workforce including Equal Opportunity Employment. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, and/or veteran status.**
**Advanced Energy is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations in our job application process/procedures for qualified individuals with disabilities. If you require assistance in completing an Advanced Energy application, please reach out to**
**HumanResources@aei.com**

identity_held_roles.description:
Shield AI is a venture-backed defense-tech company with the mission of protecting service members and civilians with intelligent systems. Its products include Hivemind autonomy software, V-BAT and X-BAT aircraft, and Aechelon simulation and synthetic reality technologies. With offices and facilities across the U.S., Europe, the Middle East, and Asia-Pacific, Shield AI’s technology actively supports operations worldwide. For more information, visit www.shield.ai. Follow Shield AI on LinkedIn, X, Instagram, and YouTube.
 
 
**Job Description**
The Senior Manager of Quality is responsible for establishing and leading all quality activities for a complex aerospace development program from prototype through production readiness. This role serves as the primary quality leader embedded within the program team and partners closely with Engineering, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, Flight Test, and Program Management to ensure products are designed, developed, tested, and transitioned to production with quality, reliability, and mission success as foundational objectives.
 
 
The Senior Manager of Quality will build and lead a multidisciplinary quality team while implementing scalable quality systems, risk management processes, problem-solving disciplines, and development quality practices appropriate for a rapidly growing aerospace and defense technology organization.
 
 
This position requires balancing speed of development with disciplined engineering rigor to support aggressive program schedules while ensuring compliance with customer, regulatory, and company requirements.
 
 
**What You'll Do**

* Development Quality Leadership
* Serve as the quality leader for XBAT development.
* Establish quality strategy, objectives, and metrics aligned with program milestones.
* Integrate quality requirements into the product development lifecycle.
* Ensure quality considerations are incorporated during system architecture, design reviews, verification, validation, and qualification activities.
* Partner with Engineering leadership to identify and mitigate technical and programmatic risks.
* Drive a culture of proactive quality and continuous improvement throughout the program.

**Design & Configuration Quality**

* Ensure quality requirements are appropriately captured in product definitions, specifications, and design documentation.
* Participate in design reviews, change control boards, and configuration management activities.
* Ensure full configuration and traceability for all material installed into prototype aircraft.
* Evaluate engineering changes for quality and production readiness impacts.
* Support requirements verification and validation planning.
* Drive design-for-manufacturing, design-for-quality, and design-for-reliability initiatives.

**Risk Management & Reliability**

* Lead quality participation in program risk management activities.
* Establish and maintain FRACAS processes for development and flight test phases of the program.
* Facilitate root cause and corrective action investigations for design, manufacturing, supplier, and field failures.
* Support reliability growth planning and execution.
* Monitor defect trends, failure modes, and reliability metrics to identify systemic risks.

**Verification, Validation & Test Quality**

* Develop quality oversight strategies for laboratory, ground, and flight test activities.
* Ensure test results, anomalies, and nonconformances are appropriately documented and dispositioned.
* Support qualification and certification efforts.
* Establish processes for managing test escapes, failures, and corrective actions.

**Nonconformance & Corrective Action Management**

* Lead Material Review Board activities for development hardware.
* Establish scalable processes for nonconformance management.
* Drive root cause analysis using structured problem-solving methodologies.
* Ensure timely and effective corrective and preventive actions.
* Track effectiveness of corrective actions through closure.

**Production Readiness & Industrialization**

* Partner with Manufacturing and Supply Chain teams to transition products from prototype to production.
* Define quality requirements for production readiness reviews.
* Support development of inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and control strategies.
* Ensure lessons learned from development are incorporated into production processes.
* Lead quality planning activities supporting low-rate initial production and rate increases.

**Quality Management System**

* Develop and implement quality processes supporting aerospace development programs.
* Ensure compliance with AS9100, customer requirements, and internal procedures.
* Drive continuous improvement of development quality processes.
* Support internal and external audits as required.
* Establish scalable systems that support future production growth.

**Leadership & Team Development**

* Build, lead, and mentor a high-performing quality organization.
* Recruit and develop quality engineers, inspectors, and technicians.
* Establish clear objectives, priorities, and performance expectations.
* Promote a culture of accountability, technical excellence, and collaboration.
* Develop organizational capabilities to support future company growth.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality, Manufacturing, Aerospace Engineering, or related technical discipline.
* 10+ years of experience in aerospace, defense, aviation, space, or other highly regulated industries.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing technical quality organizations.
* Experience supporting complex product development programs from concept through production transition.
* Strong knowledge of quality systems, engineering development processes, and aerospace manufacturing.
* Experience leading root cause investigations and corrective action programs.
* Experience with risk management, reliability engineering, and failure analysis.
* Working knowledge of AS9100 quality management systems.
* Demonstrated ability to influence cross-functional teams and senior leadership.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience supporting UAV, aerospace, defense, aviation, autonomous systems, or advanced technology programs.
* Experience leading quality organizations during rapid company growth.
* Background in systems engineering, reliability engineering, or development engineering.
* Experience with flight test programs and qualification testing.
* ASQ Certified Quality Engineer (CQE), Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence (CMQ/OE), or equivalent certification.
* Familiarity with government defense programs and customer quality requirements.

#LE
 
 
**Full-time Regular Employee Offer Package**
Pay within range listed + Bonus + Benefits + Equity
 
 
**Temporary Employee Offer Package**
Pay within range listed above + temporary benefits package (applicable after 60 days of employment)
 
 
Salary compensation is influenced by a wide array of factors including but not limited to skill set, level of experience, licenses and certifications, and specific work location. All offers are contingent on a cleared background and possible reference check. Military fellows and part-time employees are not eligible for benefits. Please speak to your talent acquisition representative for more information.
 
 
###
 
 
Shield AI is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace and is an affirmative action employer. We are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, marital status, disability, gender identity or Veteran status. If you have a disability or special need that requires accommodation, please let us know.
 
 
Compensation Range: $162,243 - $243,365

identity_held_roles.title: Sr Manager, Supplier Quality
identity_held_roles.description:
**Work Schedule**
Standard (Mon-Fri)
 
 
**Environmental Conditions**
Office
 
 
As part of the Thermo Fisher Scientific team, you'll discover meaningful work that makes a positive impact on a global scale. Join our colleagues in bringing our Mission to life every single day to enable our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer. We provide our global teams with the resources needed to achieve individual career goals while helping to take science a step beyond by developing solutions for some of the world's toughest challenges, like protecting the environment, making sure our food is safe or helping find cures for cancer.
 
 
**What will you do?**
As a Senior Manager of Supplier Quality, you'll guide our global performance management program and elevate our supplier quality standards. You'll lead a team of Supplier Quality Engineers and work closely with cross-functional partners to support continuous improvement and strategic supplier development. This role offers the opportunity to contribute to critical quality initiatives, develop partnerships with key stakeholders, and facilitate problem-solving activities that address non-conformances.
 
 
Key responsibilities include:
 
 

* Lead and develop the Supplier Quality team; build talent and succession plans, strengthen organizational capabilities, and manage performance against business priorities.
* Manage team performance through ongoing coaching and formal performance reviews; identify development needs and support individual development plans.
* Own the supplier quality framework across the supplier lifecycle, from initial assessment and qualification through ongoing monitoring and improvement.
* Assist in setting the direction for the Supplier Quality organization, translating business and quality priorities into team objectives, operating plans, and clear accountability.
* Accountable for regulatory compliance and supplier risk management, ensuring risks are assessed, prioritized, and addressed across the supply chain.
* Define supplier quality metrics and review performance trends to guide priorities, resource allocation, new technologies, and process improvements.
* Drive the adoption of technologies and processes that strengthen supplier oversight and support material qualification, product changes, and sustaining engineering.
* Oversee quality improvement programs that deliver measurable gains in supplier performance and product quality.
* Using data analysis, quality tools, project management, and professional skills, lead initiatives to enhance supplier performance and product quality.
* Build strategic alignment across Sourcing, Manufacturing, Product Engineering, Global Technical Support, Operations, and Commodity Management to resolve systemic supplier quality challenges.
* Develop senior-level supplier relationships and engage supplier leadership in addressing systemic issues and improving quality capability.
* Plan and lead supplier quality audits, document findings, and follow up on corrective actions.
* Own the supplier audit program and corrective action governance, ensuring findings are addressed and recurring issues are prevented.
* Oversee the supplier nonconformance and corrective action system, ensuring timely containment, effective root cause analysis, and sustained corrective and preventive actions.
* Guide continuous improvement priorities across the supplier network, aligning projects and resources with business needs and quality risks.
* Maintain and analyze supplier quality and performance metrics to identify trends, investigate non-conformances, and conduct root cause analysis.
* Lead continuous improvement projects that improve supplier performance and product quality.
* undefined

**How will you get there?**

* Bachelor’s Degree plus 8-10 years of experience, or Advanced Degree plus 6 years of experience in medical device/pharmaceutical industry quality or regulatory affairs roles
* Preferred fields of study: Engineering, Operations Management, or Biological Sciences
* Quality Lead Auditor certification preferred
* Minimum 3 years people management experience
* Strong knowledge of ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820 regulations
* Experience with global regulatory agencies (FDA, IVDR Notified Bodies, PMDA, ANVISA, Health Canada)
* Proficiency in Six Sigma methodologies (8D, FMEA, DMAIC, Value Stream Mapping, Pareto Analysis)
* Statistical analysis skills (SPC, DOE, sampling)
* Experience with quality management systems (SAP, TrackWise)
* Strong understanding of supplier performance management principles
* Excellence in oral and written communication, with fluency in English
* Experience implementing global harmonization initiatives
* Experience managing matrix organizations across diverse cultures
* Strong project management and strategic planning capabilities
* Ability to build and maintain relationships with internal/external stakeholders
* Willingness to travel up to 50% domestically and internationally
* Ability to work in manufacturing environments requiring PPE including cleanroom gear
* Technical proficiency with IT databases and digital tools
* Problem-solving mindset with experience implementing effective solutions
* Manage a team and provide leadership and accountability for team performance, workload prioritization, management reviews, escalated supplier risks, supplier governance cadence, KPI targets, talent development, and execution of the supplier quality strategy.
* Execute on cross-division harmonization and organizational capabilities.
* Experience working with commodities ranging from machined parts, electrical components, plastics, resin, chemicals

**About Us**
Centric Brands is a leading lifestyle brand collective that designs, sources, markets and sells high quality products in multiple segments, including women’s, men’s and kid’s apparel, accessories, entertainment and beauty. Centric Brands is focused on our customers and our brands that will drive the company’s future growth. We are defined by innovation as we seize new opportunities and thrive in an environment informed by creativity and thinking that is both analytical and outside the box. Centric Brands reflects a team built on respect, for others and for the ha rd work it takes to achieve our goals and build our bright future together.
 
 
**Product Development**
From sourcing raw material s to manufacturing, order placement, pricing, quality control and getting the finished product where it needs to be, our production/product development team is responsible for ensuring we keep our standards high and our business profitable at every step of the journey. If you are a focused, results-driven, tenacious and highly flexible team player, we’ll give you every opportunity to build a rewarding career with one of the world’s foremost major lifestyle brand collectives.
 
 
**Specific Responsibilities Would Include**
The Director, Sourcing and Product Development reports to the VP of Production for Robert Graham/Saks and will drive seasonal product initiatives by partnering with cross-functional teams, including Production, Design, Sales, and Overseas Offices, to develop and execute assigned product lines. The role primarily focuses on apparel development, with additional responsibility for trims and packaging across Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue Private Label.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Own and manage all aspects of the product development process, from concept and inspiration through quality assurance of finished goods to the end customer.
* Establish shared qualities and fabrics between Robert Graham and Saks Fifth Avenue to ensure alignment across brands.
* Partner closely with overseas hubs and vendor teams to ensure understanding of departmental objectives and leverage vendor capabilities to drive initiatives that expand competencies as needed.
* Analyze product costs, identifying opportunities and collaborating cross-functionally to create solutions through product engineering that maximize product value while accounting for cost impact.
* Oversee cross-functional milestone performance; communicate risks, deadlines, and business impacts when deliverables are at risk.
* Lead vendor sourcing initiatives aligned with driving innovation and service within the overall sourcing strategy.
* Manage new vendor onboarding and ensure all internal partners are connected and prepared to support production needs.
* Facilitate vendor meetings to review in-season development, production, and delivery challenges, and drive solutions.
* Identify business risks and opportunities, escalate appropriately, and propose actionable recommendations for improvement.
* Collaborate closely with Design and Merchandising on product creation from concept to execution, utilizing budget and SKU plans.
* Create and maintain comprehensive material and product libraries with detailed product attributes and testing documentation.

**Our Best Fit Candidate Would Have**

* Proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, Outlook); advanced Adobe, Photoshop and Illustrator skills required
* SAP experience preferred
* Excellent organizational, written, and verbal communication skills
* Strong team orientation and ability to work cross-functionally
* Ability to multitask, prioritize, and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment
* High attention to detail and accuracy
* Knowledge of garment manufacturing, construction, and fabrication

Salary Range: $125,000 - $145,000
 
 
At Centric Brands, we believe our people are our greatest asset, and we seek to structure competitive compensation offers to ensure that we are able to attract and retain the best talent. Our job postings include an annual base salary range at the time of employment. The stated base salary range represents our good faith estimate as to what candidates are likely to expect, and we tailor our offers within the range based on several factors, including the selected candidate's educational and professional experience, industry knowledge, location, technical and communication skills, and other factors that may prove relevant during the selection process. Base salary is a part of a total compensation package, which, depending on the position, may also include commission earnings, annual bonus and other Centric Brands sponsored benefit programs.
 
 
**Be part of our growing community by getting involved with groups, teams and initiatives like Be Green, Be Giving, and Be Celebrated.**
**Centric Brands is an Equal Opportunity Employer**
Please note that Centric Brands will only reach out to interview, make an offer of employment or conduct onboarding activities for candidates who have applied through our careers site. When interviewing for a position, the candidate experience will include live interaction, such as a video conference or telephone call, with a Recruiter and/or company employee(s). We will never ask for any money or payments from applicants at any point in the recruitment process. Be aware of suspicious recruitment activity. If you think you are a victim of an employment scam, you may contact your local law enforcement agency and/or visit the Federal Trade Commission website here: https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams .

identity_held_roles.description:
Work Model: This role can be performed remotely from an approved location, with flexibility based on business needs and applicable requirements.
 
 
\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_
 
 
Regal Rexnord Business System (“RBS”) plays a pivotal role in driving organizational change and process improvement to achieve our business objectives. The
**Linear Motion Division**
(“LMD”) within the AMC segment is seeking a
**Director of RBS**
. Reporting to the President of the Division, this position will drive the implementation, maturity, and cultural adoption of RBS and continuous process improvement across the division.
 
 
This leadership position is focused on the deployment of RBS across the Division to drive both short and long-term goals and will partner closely with LMD’s leadership team, as well as the AMC RBS team. The right candidate will drive operational excellence, develop CI capability, and ensure alignment to strategic priorities through Policy Deployment. This leader influences across manufacturing sites, functional teams, and the broader AMC organization to deliver year-over-year performance improvement. As a key member of the AMC RBS Team, this role will impact results and culture by establishing standards, institutionalizing management systems and ensuring effective problem-solving skills (& tool capability) across the organization.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
 
**Continuous Improvement Leadership and Standard Work**

* Champion the Lean philosophy and its deployment across all functions and manufacturing sites.
* Support the organization in achieving SQDCG and financial objectives through effective application of the RBS tools and methodologies to achieve continuous improvement.
* Develop and drive the divisional CI Roadmap and ensure alignment to site-level plans.
* Lead, guide, and help create solutions for highly complex and multi-faceted problems requiring ingenuity, creativity, innovation, and strong analytical skills. Problems are unique and require a thorough understanding of operating unit policies and practices. Apply knowledge of different techniques and practices to achieve desired results
* Connect operational improvements (e.g., machine productivity, labor productivity, lead time/turnaround time, quality, backlog, capacity, OEE, etc.) to financial outcomes (Revenue/TVOS, Cost, Cash, Margin).
* Participate in the hiring, development and coaching of site continuous improvement leaders.
* Utilize a team-oriented structured problem-solving approach to analyze current conditions, diagnose problems, and identify improvement opportunities.

**Capability and Talent Development**

* Support Division and Site RBS leaders in maturing the Regal Rexnord Business System through the development of skills, capabilities, and engagement driving impact to the next level.
* Coach, mentor, and train Regal Rexnord associates on CI tools and Lean leadership.
* Develop RBS capability through formal training and “stop-and-teach” coaching at Gemba.
* Lead and coach multiple projects and Kaizen events simultaneously through both a hands-on and influential approach.
* Engage and influence teams at all levels to drive momentum toward the future state.
* Identify, coach, and develop talent; build a strong bench of RBS tool champions across the division to leverage RBS Continuous Improvement tools and methodologies to support their professional advancement and improve the business's operational performance.

**Policy Deployment**

* Lead the creation of annual X-Matrix and oversee the deployment plan via RBS charters, bowlers, and action plans.
* Manage charters, bowlers, action plans and monthly PD cadence.
* Support Division Annual Improvement Priorities through effective application of RBS tools and methodologies to support Policy Deployment initiatives.

**Qualifications**
**PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE/QUALIFICATIONS**

* Bachelor’s degree in a technical field; Advanced degree preferred (MS Engineering, MBA)
* 8-10 years relevant work experience across Continuous Improvement, Business Systems, or Operations (global and/or multi-site experience preferred)
* Familiarity with Policy Deployment, its facilitation and implementation.
* Technical background in continuous improvement methodology and framework
* Proven successful applications of multiple CI tools: 80/20, Lean Leadership, including Daily Management, KPI Leadership, Standard Work, Gemba Walks, Value Stream Mapping, 6S, Transactional Process Improvements, Kanban/replenishment systems, FMEA, Advanced Problem Solving, RCCMs
* Demonstrated ability to facilitate Kaizen-type events to produce measurable improvements (financial, service, quality, etc.)
* Skilled and experienced in decomposing a strategic vision into actionable strategies and tactics.
* Critical thinking skills to properly identify problem area & potential solutions
* Demonstrate the Regal Rexnord Values; Integrity, Responsibility, Diversity, Engagement & Inclusion, Customer Success, Innovation with Purpose, Continuous Improvement, Performance, Passion to Win, and Sense of Urgency
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities independently.
* Must be able to travel at least 50-75% of the time domestically and internationally as required

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Project and program management expertise (PMP, Prince II)
* Lean Six Sigma certification (e.g, Green Belt or Black Belt)
* Experience with High Mix / Low Volume and Low Mix / High Volume manufacturing

Physical Demand and Work Environment
 
 
**Physical Demands**
– while performing the duties in this job, the employee is regularly required to use hands; reach with hands and arms; and talk and hear. The employee is frequently required to stand, walk, and sit.
 
 
**Work Environment**
– the noise level in the work environment is usually moderate.
 
 
Restrictions imposed by federal export control laws may limit this job opportunity to candidates who are a "U.S. Person,' which includes U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, U.S. permanent residents, individuals granted asylum in the United States, and refugees in the United States.
 
 
Expected salary: $160,000 - $190,000 annually. The salary range provided is intended to display the value of the company's base pay compensation for all statewide locations across the United States. Salary is dependent on a multitude of factors, including but not limited to the physical worksite location, candidate's skill set, level of experience, education, and internal peer compensation comparisons.
 
 
**Benefits**

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Prescription Drug Coverage
* Spending accounts (HSA, Health Care FSA and Dependent Care FSA)
* Paid Time Off and Holidays
* 401k Retirement Plan with Matching Employer Contributions
* Life and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) Insurance
* Paid Leaves
* Tuition Assistance

**About Regal Rexnord**
Regal Rexnord is a publicly held global industrial manufacturer with 30,000 associates around the world who help create a better tomorrow by providing sustainable solutions that power, transmit and control motion. The Company’s electric motors and air moving subsystems provide the power to create motion. A portfolio of highly engineered power transmission components and subsystems efficiently transmits motion to power industrial applications. The Company’s automation offering, comprised of controls, actuators, drives, and precision motors, controls motion in applications ranging from factory automation to precision control in surgical tools.
 
 
The Company’s end markets benefit from meaningful secular demand tailwinds, and include factory automation, food & beverage, aerospace, medical, data center, warehouse, alternative energy, residential and commercial buildings, general industrial, construction, metals and mining, and agriculture.
 
 
Regal Rexnord is comprised of three operating segments: Industrial Powertrain Solutions, Power Efficiency Solutions, and Automation & Motion Control. Regal Rexnord has offices and manufacturing, sales and service facilities worldwide. For more information, including a copy of our Sustainability Report, visit RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
**Equal Employment Opportunity Statement**
Regal Rexnord is an Equal Opportunity and Affirmative Action Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex/gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, pregnancy, age, ancestry, national origin, genetic information, marital status, citizenship status (unless required by the applicable law or government contract), disability or protected veteran status or any other status or characteristic protected by law. Regal Rexnord is committed to a diverse and inclusive workforce. We are committed to building a team that represents diverse and inclusive backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. If you’d like to view a copy of the company’s affirmative action plan for protected veterans/individuals with disabilities or policy statement, please email Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com. If you have a disability and you believe you need a reasonable accommodation in order to search for a job opening or to submit an online application, please e-mail Recruiting@RegalRexnord.com.
 
 
Equal Employment Opportunity Posters
 
 
**Notification to Agencies**
: Please note that Regal Rexnord Corporation and its affiliates and subsidiaries ("Regal Rexnord") do not accept unsolicited resumes or calls from third-party recruiters or employment agencies. In the absence of a signed Master Service Agreement or similar contract and approval from HR to submit resumes for a specific requisition, Regal Rexnord will not consider or approve payment to any third-parties for hires made.

**Description**
**Alvarez & Marsal Private Equity Performance Improvement**
**Director: Operations & Manufacturing**
**(OPEN TO ALL U.S. LOCATIONS)**
**About Alvarez & Marsal**
Alvarez & Marsal (A&M) is a global consulting firm with over 13,000 entrepreneurial, action and results-oriented professionals in over 40 countries. We take a hands-on approach to solving our clients' problems and assisting them in reaching their potential. Our culture celebrates independent thinkers and doers who positively impact our clients and shape our industry. The collaborative environment and engaging work—guided by A&M's core values of Integrity, Quality, Objectivity, Fun, Personal Reward, and Inclusive Diversity—are why our people love working at A&M.
 
 
**The Team**
A&M’s Private Equity Performance Improvement Services (PEPI) practice, with offices throughout the US, focuses on serving the middle market and large cap private equity firms who have engaged A&M to help improve operating results at their portfolio companies.
 
 
Our professionals are aligned with a PEPI service line to promote the development of deep functional skills & experiences and to maximize our ability to tailor solutions to solve our clients' business issues.
 
 
We bring a structured and disciplined approach to create and capture value. We provide private equity clients with a broad continuum of knowledge and tools for cost improvements, transformations, mergers, acquisitions, and carve-outs.
 
 
A&M’s Operations professionals assist our clients in analyzing
**manufacturing operations**
, supply chain and distribution channels, procurement, SG&A operations, and sales force effectiveness for potential value creation opportunities and help drive them during our client’s ownership. From our thorough fact-based analysis, we assess the state of operations, identify key risks to investment and quantify potential EBITDA improvement plans for the buyer and seller.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Who We Are**
Applied Materials is a global leader in materials engineering solutions used to produce virtually every new chip and advanced display in the world. We design, build and service cutting-edge equipment that helps our customers manufacture display and semiconductor chips – the brains of devices we use every day. As the foundation of the global electronics industry, Applied enables the exciting technologies that literally connect our world – like AI and IoT. If you want to push the boundaries of materials science and engineering to create next generation technology, join us to deliver material innovation that changes the world.
 
 
**What We Offer**
Salary:
 
 
$168,000.00 - $231,000.00
 
 
Location:
 
 
Santa Clara,CA
 
 
You’ll benefit from a supportive work culture that encourages you to learn, develop, and grow your career as you take on challenges and drive innovative solutions for our customers. We empower our team to push the boundaries of what is possible—while learning every day in a supportive leading global company. Visit our Careers website to learn more.
 
 
At Applied Materials, we care about the health and wellbeing of our employees. We’re committed to providing programs and support that encourage personal and professional growth and care for you at work, at home, or wherever you may go. Learn more about our benefits.
 
 
**What You'll Do**
Be a part of internal consulting team with high visibility to Applied Global Services executive leadership. Lead strategic projects to streamline business processes, improve supply chain and operations, reduce costs, and improve business performance through advanced analytics. Have responsibility for complete project life cycle starting with analysis of the as-is process, identification and quantification of the opportunities, development of improvement streams, securing buy-in from stakeholders, and driving implementation.
 
 
High impact role that requires relentless change management motivation rewarded with material impact to business unit performance.
 
 
**Key Responsibilities**

* Structure and break down complex business problems, develop hypothesis, drive analysis and deliver data-driven recommendations
* Lead thoughtful and rigorous analysis across large data sets and synthesize insights and opportunities
* Develop and present high-quality recommendation and deliverables for executive level consumption and contribute to associated strategy and execution discussions
* Work collaboratively across a cross-functional set of stakeholders to gather the right information, pressure test your hypothesis, co-create deliverables, accelerate execution and unlock value
* Optimize operations and business process to improve performance, reduce cycle time, and shrink costs

**Qualifications**

* Industrial Engineering or equivalent Bachelor degree. MBA preferred
* 10+ years relevant work experience
* Semiconductor experience preferred
* Management consulting experience preferred
* Broad understanding and experience including logistics, financial reporting, operations, and service business management.
* Strong analytical skills – able to extract real insight from multiple data sources
* Excellent oral and written communication, organizational, analytical, and interpersonal skills
* Able to work effectively in a matrix environment and influence others
* Detail oriented, able to connect the dots and communicate complex ideas effectively
* Knowledge of Lean / Six Sigma

**Additional Information**
**Time Type:**
Full time
 
 
**Employee Type:**
Assignee / Regular
 
 
**Travel:**
Yes, 10% of the Time
 
 
**Relocation Eligible:**
Yes
 
 
The salary offered to a selected candidate will be based on multiple factors including location, hire grade, job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and with consideration of internal equity of our current team members. In addition to a comprehensive benefits package, candidates may be eligible for other forms of compensation such as participation in a bonus and a stock award program, as applicable.
 
 
For all sales roles, the posted salary range is the Target Total Cash (TTC) range for the role, which is the sum of base salary and target bonus amount at 100% goal achievement.
 
 
Applied Materials is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, national origin, citizenship, ancestry, religion, creed, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, disability, veteran or military status, or any other basis prohibited by law.
 
 
In addition, Applied endeavors to make our careers site accessible to all users. If you would like to contact us regarding accessibility of our website or need assistance completing the application process, please contact us via e-mail at Accommodations\_Program@amat.com, or by calling our HR Direct Help Line at 877-612-7547, option 1, and following the prompts to speak to an HR Advisor. This contact is for accommodation requests only and cannot be used to inquire about the status of applications.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Position Title:**
Director of Operations

**Reports to:**
General Manager

**Location:**
Gallatin, TN (Division HQ)

**Direct Reports:**
9

**The Opportunity**

Our client is a division of a Fortune 500 diversified industrial manufacturer with roughly $14B in global revenue, operations in 57 countries, and a portfolio of more than 16,000 active patents. Within that global enterprise, this division is a focused, ~$160M automotive business serving major OEMs and Tier suppliers across North America, leveraging deep-draw stamping technologies and decades of application engineering expertise.

The division operates multiple manufacturing and distribution sites across the Southeast and Northeast, anchored by its headquarters and primary manufacturing campus in Gallatin, TN. As the business enters its next chapter — capability modernization, and renewed organic growth — it needs an Operations leader who can run the business of today while building the business of tomorrow.

**Lead a transformation. Build a legacy. Own the outcome.**

This is not a caretaker role. It's a rare, high-visibility opportunity to step into a growing, profitable business backed by the resources, stability, and global reach of a Fortune 500 diversified industrial manufacturer — and to personally shape what it becomes next. You'll inherit a division with a 35+ year manufacturing legacy, a loyal and deeply experienced workforce, and a clear mandate for bold operational transformation: optimizing operations, modernizing the labor model for a new generation of talent, and forging a tighter bond between Operations and Commercial to fuel organic growth. If you want a role where the runway is wide open and the impact is yours to claim, keep reading.

**Why This Role Is Different**

* High-impact, transformational mandate — this is a newly elevated role with the charter and authority to truly take ownership of the business, not just maintain it
* Backed by Fortune 500 scale — decentralized, entrepreneurial autonomy at the division level, paired with the resources, tools, and career runway of a global industrial leader
* Clear, visible wins available — from operational execution to building a 21st-century labor model to deepening customer intimacy, the opportunities to make your mark here are numerous and tangible
* A proven leadership pipeline — division-level operating roles within this organization are widely recognized as launching pads for senior General Manager and executive careers
* A business, not a project — you'll own real P&L-relevant outcomes: safety, quality, delivery, cost, and growth, with a seat at the Division Leadership table

**What You'll Own**

Operations Strategy & Business Leadership

* Develop and execute the division's operations strategy in direct alignment with business and growth objectives
* Lead multi-site manufacturing operations to deliver growth, customer satisfaction, and profitability
* Drive the optimization of the manufacturing footprint, building a clear current-state → future-state → glide-path plan that brings the organization along rather than alienating it
* Partner closely with Commercial, Engineering, Supply Chain, Finance, and HR to ensure operations and growth strategy move in lockstep
* Serve as a key voice on the Division Leadership Team, directly shaping strategic decisions

Operational Excellence & Continuous Improvement

* Champion enterprise-proven operational excellence principles and an 80/20 prioritization mindset across every site
* Lead initiatives that meaningfully move the needle on safety, quality, delivery, productivity, and cost
* Build scalable systems, management routines, and standard work that sustain results long after you've moved on to the next challenge
* Diagnose performance gaps quickly and drive disciplined, data-backed corrective action — the General Manager you'll partner with is an engineer who loves data
* Champion simplification, standardization, and value-stream optimization across a business proud of its craft but ready to evolve

People Leadership & Organizational Capability

* Lead and develop a team of 9 direct reports, including a Plant Manager, two Production Managers, and functional leaders in Quality, Maintenance, Tooling, Supply Chain, Sourcing, and Customer Relations — a true leader of leaders
* Build bench strength through succession planning, leadership development, and workforce planning, especially as long-tenured talent approaches retirement
* Modernize the labor model for a new generation of manufacturing talent — understanding what today's workforce values, and building a culture that earns their best
* Capture and institutionalize decades of hands-on process knowledge before it walks out the door, while bringing fresh energy and accountability to the floor
* Foster a culture of ownership and continuous improvement that respects the site's proud history while embracing what's next

Financial & Operational Performance

* Own performance across safety, quality, delivery, productivity, inventory, cost, and profitability
* Lead budgeting, forecasting, capital planning, and resource allocation for the division's operations
* Establish clear performance expectations, KPIs, and accountability systems, and act decisively when results lag
* Ensure operations directly fuel profitable, sustainable growth for the business

Customer & Growth Impact

* Be the bridge between Operations and Commercial — customers increasingly want visibility into the supply chain well beyond the sales relationship, and you'll meet that need directly
* Engage with customers both digitally and in person, including early-phase new product development collaboration with the Commercial team
* Support new product launches, capacity expansion, and other growth initiatives as the division pursues new organic growth opportunities
* Lead enterprise-level projects that strengthen manufacturing and supply chain capability across the network

What Success Looks Like in Year One

* Optimization efforts are integrated smoothly, hitting expected quality, cost, and delivery targets
* Talent has been assessed at the direct-report and next level down, particularly in supervisory roles
* A modern, future-focused labor model is taking shape on the shop floor — including early steps toward integrating AI and digital tools into manufacturing processes
* A visibly stronger Operations–Commercial partnership is generating new opportunities for the facility, with Operations engaged at the technical level alongside Sales

What You Bring

* Bachelor's degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field
* 5+ years of progressive experience in operations, program management, or manufacturing leadership, ideally in a multi-site environment
* Direct experience with plant expansions and consolidations, footprint optimization, or large-scale operational change — strongly preferred
* Solid grounding in manufacturing operations, capacity planning, and supply chain flow; prior stamping experience is a plus, not a requirement, as long as you can quickly learn, interpret, and verify what your team is telling you
* A track record of leading through change with emotional intelligence — able to push for transformation without alienating a workforce with deep institutional knowledge and pride in their craft
* Strong executive presence and the ability to influence stakeholders at every level, from the plant floor to the Division Leadership Team
* Willingness to travel regularly between sites (roughly one multi-day trip per month, plus periodic site and corporate visits)

Leadership Capabilities We're Looking For

* Strategic & Operational Leadership
* Change Leadership
* Accountability & Execution Discipline
* People Development & Team Building
* Continuous Improvement & Results Orientation

**Why You'll Want to Stay**

This division offers what's rare in manufacturing leadership today: the backing and stability of a Fortune 500 diversified industrial manufacturer, paired with the autonomy and entrepreneurial energy of a standalone business unit. Division leadership roles within this organization are widely viewed as launching pads for the next level of senior leadership — and with a mandate this clear and this meaningful, the opportunities to leave your mark go well beyond the margins.

**About the Organization**

Our client is a Fortune 500 diversified industrial manufacturer delivering specialized expertise and value-added products across a wide range of industries worldwide. With approximately $14 billion in global revenue, operations across 57 countries, roughly 45,000 employees, and a portfolio of more than 16,000 active patents, the company is recognized as a global leader in applied engineering and manufacturing innovation.

Within this global enterprise, the business division supplies products to major automotive OEMs and Tier suppliers, leveraging deep-draw stamping technologies and decades of application engineering expertise. The division generates approximately $160M in annual revenue and operates a multi-site manufacturing and distribution network anchored by its headquarters and primary manufacturing campus in Gallatin, TN.

An Equal Opportunity / Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, or protected veteran status.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description:**

**Who We Are:**

At Cart.com, we're **defining the future of commerce.**

Founded to solve the growing complexity of modern commerce, Cart.com helps businesses simplify how they sell, fulfill, and deliver products to their customers. We bring together technology, services, and logistics infrastructure into one connected platform, making it easier for organizations to grow, operate efficiently, and navigate an increasingly fragmented commerce landscape.

We work with brands, retailers, manufacturers, and public sector organizations to support every stage of the customer journey, from ecommerce and order management to fulfillment, distribution, and delivery. By combining software, expertise, and a nationwide logistics network into a unified solution, we help our customers move faster, operate smarter, and scale with confidence.

But what truly sets Cart.com apart is our people. We're builders, problem-solvers, and innovators who thrive on turning big challenges into meaningful outcomes for our customers. Every day, we're helping shape the future of commerce while creating opportunities to learn, grow, and make an impact.

If you're energized by solving complex problems, collaborating with talented teammates, and helping build what's next, we'd love to hear from you.

**Cart.com Milestones**

* Founded in 2020 with a vision to build the first truly unified commerce platform.
* Achieved unicorn status with a valuation exceeding $1 billion.
* Raised more than $475 million to support continued growth and innovation
* Expanded a nationwide commerce and logistics network that helps organizations scale, fulfill, and grow across channels.
* Recognized by Inc.'s Power Partner Awards for helping businesses grow and scale.
* Recognized as an award-winning employer for four consecutive years, reflecting our commitment to building an environment where talented people can grow, innovate, and make an impact.

**Our values:** Cart.com is building a company that is committed to living out these 6 core values:

* **Be brand obsessed:** Our lives are shaped by the brands we interact with daily. We obsess over the brands we serve, and about the things they care about.
* **Think beyond the box:** “We’ve always done it that way” is not a phrase uttered often at our office. We create creative solutions to complex problems.

* **Don’t give up:** We learn from our challenges and see them for what they are; great building blocks to an amazing brand story.
* **Speak up:** We communicate clearly and directly because we care deeply. Communication is the bedrock of our community.
* **Work together:** We’ve built a team that prides itself on diversity of thought and background. Collaboration is better with contrast.
* **Remember to be human:** We work hard, but we leave room for the people, places and things that we love

**AI is part of how we work. It's not doing the hiring.** 
 
We'll use AI in parts of our process and we think you should feel free to use it too — for research, prep, whatever helps. But our interviews exist to meet *you*, not your best AI-assisted draft. Real people make every call here. Any questions about how this works, just ask.

**Remote:**

This position is fully remote and open to candidates in AZ, CA, CO, CT, DC, DE, FL, GA, HI, IL, IN, KY, LA, MA, MD, MI, MO, MS, NC, NJ, NY, NC, OH, OR, PA, SC, TN, TX, UT, VA, WA. The salary range for this role is $175,000-200,000 annually. Actual compensation may vary based on geographic location, experience and qualifications. This role is eligible for bonus, equity and benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), paid time off. Applications accepted through 1-31-2027. We comply with all applicable pay transparency laws in the states where we operate.

**The Role:**

The Director, Quality and Compliance leads the quality function for Cart.com’s federal pharmaceutical distribution business across four sites. This leader will standardize and strengthen an established quality program, develop site quality leaders, ensure consistent application of procedures, and serve as the primary quality point of contact for client reporting, audits and product-quality events.

This is approximately a 70% strategic leadership and 30% hands-on role. The Director will not build the program from the ground up, but will assess the current-state program, make targeted improvements, and ensure teams consistently execute against client, regulatory and network requirements. The role is remote with approximately 30% travel.

The role offers the opportunity to influence the quality standard for a growing federal business and help prepare the organization to support additional federal programs over time.

**What You’ll Do**

* Lead and develop site quality leaders across Maryland, Goodyear, Temecula and Memphis, establishing clear accountability, delegation and follow-through.
* Standardize quality procedures and expectations across the network while refining the existing quality management system and closing identified gaps.
* Ensure sites remain prepared for client and regulatory audits; support audit planning, host or coordinate inspections, and oversee timely responses and corrective actions.
* Serve as the primary quality point of contact for pharmaceutical product excursions and related client reporting, ensuring submissions are accurate, complete and timely.
* Oversee quality processes supporting receiving, quarantine, release, disposition, returns, destruction, recalls, deviations, corrective and preventive actions, change control, training, complaints and document control.
* Guide quality decisions for controlled-temperature pharmaceutical products, including refrigerated, frozen and ultra-cold storage and distribution.
* Partner with site Operations leaders and Cart.com’s Compliance team to implement operational changes required to meet quality standards and client expectations.
* Use quality metrics, audit findings, client feedback and site observations to identify risk, prioritize improvements and report progress to senior leadership.
* Travel to sites for audit preparation, team development, quality reviews and issue resolution.

**Who You Are:**

 

* You are a strategic, hands-on quality leader who can set direction while stepping into audits, excursions and site-readiness work when needed.
* You lead through others, delegate clearly, establish checkpoints and hold site quality leaders accountable for follow-through.
* You put the client’s requirements first, ask the right questions and respond with accurate, timely information.
* You communicate with credibility and composure across clients, regulators, Operations, Compliance and senior leadership.
* You are highly organized and disciplined, ensuring commitments, documentation and escalations do not get lost.
* You build strong cross-functional partnerships and can influence operational changes without creating a separate quality silo.
* You adapt to changing federal-client requirements while maintaining consistent quality standards and sound judgment.
* You develop people, address performance gaps directly and create a culture of ownership across a distributed team.

**What You’ve Done:**

 

* 7+ years of progressive pharmaceutical quality experience, including work in a current Good Manufacturing Practice (cGMP) facility and meaningful pharmaceutical distribution, logistics or 3PL quality exposure.
* 5+ years of people-leadership experience with demonstrated success delegating, developing leaders and holding teams accountable.
* Worked in pharmaceutical distribution, wholesale, logistics or third-party logistics (3PL). Manufacturing experience alone is not sufficient without meaningful distribution-quality exposure.
* Applied cGMP, Good Distribution Practice (GDP), controlled-document and standard operating procedure requirements in a regulated pharmaceutical environment.
* Prepared for or led audits involving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration or comparable regulators, including managing responses and follow-up actions.
* Supported pharmaceutical product release, disposition, holds, recalls or temperature-excursion decisions in a regulated distribution setting.
* Written, revised or implemented quality procedures and documentation, then ensured consistent execution across teams or sites.
* Led a distributed or multi-site team and built accountability through site leaders rather than personally owning every task.
* Managed a significant client, product-quality or regulatory issue requiring coordination across Quality, Operations and Compliance.
* Earned a bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, biology, chemistry or a related field, or bring an equivalent combination of relevant education and experience.
* Ability to travel up to 30%.

**Nice to Haves:**

 

* Background supporting federal health programs or agencies such as HHS, DLA, ASPR, BARDA, DoD or VA.
* Experience with pharmaceutical 3PLs, wholesalers, state licensing or NABP accreditation.
* Hands-on experience with vaccines or other cold-chain and ultra-cold pharmaceutical products.
* Knowledge of Drug Supply Chain Security Act requirements and suspect or illegitimate product processes.
* Relevant certifications such as ASQ Certified Quality Auditor, Certified Manager of Quality/Organizational Excellence, Certified Pharmaceutical GMP Professional or Lead Auditor.
* Master’s degree in a life-sciences or related discipline.
Direct leadership of quality teams 

 
 

**Physical Demands & Working Conditions:**

 

* Remote work environment with regular computer and video-conference use.
* Ability to travel by air or ground up to 30% and work onsite in warehouse, pharmaceutical distribution and temperature-controlled environments.
* Ability to move through operating areas and wear required personal protective equipment when visiting sites.
* Flexibility to support audits, client needs or quality events outside standard business hours when required.

Eligibility Requirement: This position is open only to U.S. citizens due to applicable federal requirements. By applying, you confirm that you are a U.S. citizen and can provide acceptable documentation verifying your status if selected. 
 
If you are not a U.S. citizen, please do not apply for this role.

Cart.com is an equal opportunity employer. We celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.

identity_held_roles.title: Director of Quality Assurance
identity_held_roles.description:
As the Regional Director of Food Safety & Quality Assurance, you will be responsible for overseeing and ensuring the highest standards of food safety and quality across our operations in the United States and/or Canada. You will lead a team of professionals dedicated to maintaining compliance with regulatory requirements and company policies while driving continuous improvement initiatives. This role requires strong leadership, strategic thinking, and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and locations.

**Duties and Responsibilities****:**

* Ensure individual plant teams are executing expected actions to meet corporate objectives
* Manages assigned plant FS-Q managers, and interacts with operations, R&D, and other relevant teams to implement the company’s strategic plan that encompasses all aspects of food safety and quality.
* Coaches plant FS-Q managers to ensure they perform according with strategic and the tactical/milestones necessary to achieve operational goals.
* Manages key customer (other than McDonald’s) QA relationships in conjunction with sales personnel.
* Work in partnership with direct manager to be in compliance with the regional McDonald’s FSQA expectations.
* Support and coach Plant FS-Q Managers for administering the department’s budget to ensure proper allocation of resources
* Assess and manages plant resources to ensure the QA and Food Safety KPI goals are achieved for the manufacturing plants under its purview.
* Ensures the food safety and quality of product and services by assessing compliance with product testing, performing internal assessments and audits of the FS-Q system and product lines, placing defective products on hold and taking corrective action
* Insures that all regulatory requirements are met including weights/measures, food safety, product claims, declarations, etc.
* Collaborates to standardize when required, QA policies/procedures to improve efficiency and reduce cost.
* Identifies and communicates FS- QA technologies to improve quality and reduce costs.
* Coaches and develops QA Managers to perform at a constantly exceptional level of performance, including but not limited to the sanitation program, compliance with the GFSI approved scheme audits; and when required acts as the plant’s SQF back-up Practitioner.
* Performs all other duties as assigned.

**Minimum Job Requirements:**

**Education/Certifications** **and Experience:**

* Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Microbiology, Chemistry, or related field (Master’s degree preferred).
* Minimum of five (5) years of management experience including Quality Management Systems and/or Manufacturing experience.
* Prefer experience in a bakery/dry mixing (dry blending, frozen dough and baked goods) production environment.

**Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:**

* Proficient use of computer, Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint, OneNote), and other related applications or software.
* Demonstrated leadership experience and a sense of urgency and the drive to make continuous improvements
* Ability to operate at single and multi-site levels from management to “hands on” to accomplish tasks. Must be a “working manager.”
* Demonstrated ability to make and act on decisions while balancing speed, food safety, quality and risk.
* Strong background in sanitation principles and practices, GFSI approved schemes (SQF, BRC), HACCP, GMPs, Safety and SPC.
* Ability to think clearly and in a decisive manner while remaining calm under in pressure situations.
* Excellent oral and written communication skills.
* Ability to work in a matrix environment and build strong relationships by being transparent, reliable, and accountable. Strong interpersonal skills backed-up by strong technical knowledge are critical to success in this role.
* Must have good writing skills and be able to communicate effectively with people at all levels of the company.

**Supervisory Responsibilities****:**

* Manage multiple direct reports including but not limited to: Sr. Quality Assurance Manager, Quality Assurance Manager, Analyst.
* Work requires supervising and monitoring work performance of direct reports including making final decisions on hiring and disciplinary actions, evaluating program/work objectives and effectiveness, and realigning work and staffing assignments, as needed.
* Develop functional responsibilities of individuals that report to this position and ensure that best-in class output is created.

**Working Conditions and Physical Effort:**

* Typical work in office environment but will spend periods of time in manufacturing plants which will have exposure to unusual elements, such as dirt, dust, fumes, odors, darkness and/or poor lighting, noise and vibration. Seasonal exposure to weather elements to include, but not limited to, extreme temperatures, wetness and humidity.
* Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times.
* Substantial travel required (up to 50%) mostly in the North America.

**Expectations:**

* Will demonstrate, promote, and exemplify the Company’s Core Values.

At C.H. Guenther, we value transparency in compensation. By providing the salary range for this role, we aim to promote fairness and help candidates make informed choices about their career. The salary range for this role is:

$142,500.00 - $228,000.00 USD

Actual compensation may vary based on job-related knowledge, skills, and experience, as well as geographic location.

**C.H. Guenther & Son will never offer or pay a wage or salary that is not compliant with applicable local, state, or federal pay laws, including minimum salary thresholds.**

We also offer a variety of benefits, including health and disability insurance, retirement savings options, flexible spending accounts, employee assistance programs, educational assistance, parental leave, paid time off, and company-paid holidays.

For additional information about our company, go to www.chg.com.

Click here for more information regarding E-verify.

identity_held_roles.description:
**Job Description:**
--------------------

**Job Title** Quality Assurance, Operations Support Services & Service Delivery

**Corporate Title** Director

**Location** Santa Ana, CA

**Overview**

*As a Director within Document Custody Operations, you will lead quality assurance, operations support services, and service delivery to strengthen execution, protect client and organizational interests, and improve service outcomes. You will oversee quality control, training, operational risk and controls, continuous improvement, and sustained regulatory, agency, investor, and audit readiness. As a senior operational representative and Document Custody and agency subject matter expert, you will translate agency, investor, client, contractual, and internal requirements into practical operating standards. You will partner across Operations, Client Services, control functions, Technology, and delivery partners to resolve complex issues and balance client service, efficiency, and custodial obligations.*

**What We Offer You**

* A diverse and inclusive environment that embraces change, innovation, and collaboration
* A hybrid working model, allowing for in-office / work from home flexibility, generous vacation, personal and volunteer days
* Employee Resource Groups support an inclusive workplace for everyone and promote community engagement
* Competitive compensation packages including health and wellbeing benefits, retirement savings plans, parental leave, and family building benefits
Educational resources, matching gift and volunteer programs 

**What You’ll Do**

* Own the Document Custody quality assurance framework, operating standards, governance, and controls, including maker/checker reviews, segregation of duties, approvals, system validations, and evidence requirements
* Oversee independent, risk-based quality control testing, sampling, defect tracking, root-cause analysis, corrective and preventative action, and remediation validation; report quality performance and emerging risks to senior leadership
* Lead training and knowledge-management governance, including agency and document fundamentals, competency assessments, certification standards, cross-training, and targeted retraining informed by quality findings and audit observations
* Translate Federal National Mortgage Association (FNMA), Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation (FHLMC), Government National Mortgage Association (GNMA), private investor, client, and custodial requirements into procedures and service expectations; guide collateral documentation, certification, endorsements, assignments, allonges, trailing documents, releases, reinstatements, exceptions, and inventory controls
* Lead operational support and client service delivery, including implementations, service levels, capacity planning, complex research, incidents, aging items, and escalations; balance responsiveness with contractual commitments, controls, cost, and risk appetite
Maintain audit and examination readiness, oversee findings and management action plans, and partner with Technology on workflow, automation, data, and reporting enhancements that deliver measurable improvements in quality, capacity, client outcomes, and resilience 

**How You’ll Lead**

* Lead and develop direct reports and matrixed teams across quality assurance, quality control, training, audit support, operational support, service delivery, and process improvement, establishing clear decision rights, accountability, and development objectives
* Partner with Operations, Client Services, and clients as a senior advisor and escalation point, ensuring service commitments are executable, controlled, and aligned with custodial obligations
Influence senior leadership, Audit, Risk, Compliance, Legal, Technology, vendors, and offshore partners to challenge risk decisions constructively, resolve cross-functional issues, and deliver sustainable remediation and transformation 

**Skills You’ll Need**

* Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Risk Management, Operations Management, Mortgage Banking, or a related discipline; equivalent directly relevant experience may be considered where permitted by organizational policy
* Extensive experience in document custody, mortgage banking, loan servicing, securities services, collateral management, quality assurance, operational risk, service delivery, or another highly controlled financial-services environment
* Demonstrated experience with Quality Assurance/Quality Control frameworks, control testing, issue management, root-cause analysis, corrective and preventative action, training governance, operational reporting, and client escalation management, including support for audits, client examinations, agency reviews, regulatory assessments, or formal control testing
* Knowledge of operational risk, controls, quality management, audit readiness, remediation, and service-delivery governance, with the ability to translate agency, investor, client, contractual, and internal requirements into operational standards
* Working proficiency with Microsoft 365 and experience using dashboards, workflow tools, quality trackers, case-management systems, or operational reporting platforms
Proven ability to leverage AI tools to enhance productivity, optimize workflows to solve business problems, while applying critical judgment to ensure responsible and ethical use of data and AI outputs 

**Skills That Will Help You Excel**

* Direct working knowledge of Document Custody and FNMA, FHLMC, GNMA, private investor, collateral, certification, release, and exception requirements
* Experience leading managers, professionals, programs, or complex cross-functional operating models, with the ability to influence across functions, locations, vendors, and onshore/offshore teams
* Executive presence and effective written and verbal communication with clients, auditors, senior management, control functions, and technical subject matter experts
* Analytical judgment to identify patterns, quantify operational impacts, challenge assumptions, and make risk-informed decisions
Disciplined prioritization and follow-through when managing multiple critical issues, with timely escalation of material concerns 

**Expectations**

It is the Bank’s expectation that employees hired into this role will work in the Santa Ana office in accordance with the Bank’s hybrid working model.

Deutsche Bank provides reasonable accommodations to candidates and employees with a substantiated need based on disability and/or religion.

The salary range for this position in California is $133,000 to $203,500. Actual salaries may be based on a number of factors including, but not limited to, a candidate’s skill set, experience, education, work location and other qualifications. Posted salary ranges do not include incentive compensation or any other type of remuneration.

**Deutsche Bank Benefits**

At Deutsche Bank, we recognize that our benefit programs have a profound impact on our colleagues. That’s why we are focused on providing benefits and perks that enable our colleagues to live authentically and be their whole selves, at every stage of life. We provide access to physical, emotional, and financial wellness benefits that allow our colleagues to stay financially secure and strike balance between work and home. Click here to learn more!

Learn more about your life at Deutsche Bank through the eyes of our current employees: https://careers.db.com/life

The California Consumer Privacy Act outlines how companies can use personal information. If you are interested in receiving a copy of Deutsche Bank’s California Privacy Notice please email HR.Direct@DB.com .

**#LI-HYBRID**

We strive for a culture in which we are empowered to excel together every day. This includes acting responsibly, thinking commercially, taking initiative and working collaboratively.

Together we share and celebrate the successes of our people. Together we are Deutsche Bank Group.

We welcome applications from all people and promote a positive, fair and inclusive work environment.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, protected veteran status or other characteristics protected by law. Click these links to view Deutsche Bank’s Equal Opportunity Policy Statement and the following notices: EEOC Know Your Rights ; Employee Rights and Responsibilities under the Family and Medical Leave Act ; and Employee Polygraph Protection Act .
