Dow Jones Energy is a leading global energy intelligence business providing trusted price reporting from our specialist Price Reporting Agency (PRA) OPIS, Chemical Market Analytics (CMA) and McCloskey, proprietary data, market intelligence, news and research to help customers navigate increasingly interconnected energy markets. Through our specialist businesses, Dow Jones Energy makes it easier to discover and access trusted expertise spanning oil and gas, chemicals, refined fuels, coal, electric vehicle infrastructure and renewables. Our specialist businesses combine rigorous pricing methodologies with world-class human judgment to deliver the trusted intelligence and specialist insight customers need to make confident decisions.

**About the Role**

The Director of Business Optimization & Operational Excellence will play a pivotal role in transforming commercial operations into a highly efficient, value-impacting engine. Reporting directly to the VP of Operational Excellence, this role is tasked with managing the Business Optimization team driving the end-to-end Customer Journey process improvement, strengthening commercial and commercial operations execution, and enabling sustainable business growth. In addition, implement systematic collection of VOC across customer facing functions for actionable insights.The successful candidate will leverage Lean management frameworks, process mapping methodologies, automation technologies, and advanced Salesforce CRM optimization to eliminate friction across commercial workflows. Furthermore, this role will champion cross-functional alignment and operational efficiency across critical commercial partnering functions, including Sales Excellence, Customer Service, Sales Coordination, RevOps, Marketing, Billing and Legal teams.

**You Will**

* Process Mapping, Streamlining & Lean Optimization

* Workflow Documentation: Map existing end-to-end commercial operations, creating comprehensive As-Is process maps, standard operating procedures, and To-Be future-state designs.
* Lean & Continuous Improvement: Apply Lean, Six Sigma, and Kaizen methodologies to identify operational bottlenecks, redundancies, waste, and friction points across departments.
* Optimization Execution: Redesign Lead to Cash workflows to reduce cycle times, minimize error rates, eliminate rework, and enhance overall service delivery quality.
* Customer Journey Optimization: Partner with marketing, sales and sales operations to design, evaluate, and refine automated lead journeys that nurture prospects and generate high-intent sales leads.

* Cross-Functional Support Team Operational Efficiency

**You Have**

**Experience**

* 12+ years of progressive professional experience in business operations, management consulting, or commercial operational excellence.
* 4-5+ years of direct people management, with proven success leading optimization or continuous improvement teams
* **Lean / Six Sigma:** Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification strongly preferred.

**Job Title:** Director, Enterprise Business Transformation & Operational Excellence

**Location:** Westfield, IN

**Employment Type:** Full-Time

  
  

We are seeking a hands-on transformation leader to drive enterprise-wide strategy, operating-model improvements, and value creation across a complex, multi-site industrial business. This role is a core member of the organizational leadership team, with a mandate to personally lead, structure, analyze, and execute transformation initiatives—working directly with executive leadership and cross-functional teams to turn strategy into measurable results.

  
  

This person will operate as a strategic problem solver and execution partner, identifying opportunities, building business cases, redesigning processes, and driving initiatives through implementation and value realization. For the right candidate, this role offers a clear path to building and leading a dedicated transformation team as the capability matures within the organization.

  
  

**OVERALL RESPONSIBILITIES**

* Personally lead enterprise transformation and operating-model improvement initiatives from problem definition and strategy through execution and measurable value realization.
* Analyze business performance, identify operational and financial improvement opportunities, and develop actionable recommendations.
* Drive operational excellence initiatives using Lean, Six Sigma, and continuous-improvement methodologies to improve cost, quality, safety, delivery, and profitability.
* Lead and support M&A activities, including due diligence, post-merger integration, carve-outs, and synergy/value-capture initiatives.
* Build and maintain transformation roadmaps, business cases, financial models, project plans, KPIs, and governance mechanisms.
* Work directly with commercial, finance, and operations leaders to improve P&L performance, profitable growth, and value creation.
* Identify opportunities to modernize core systems and processes, including ERP/SAP, and evaluate AI-enabled and digital solutions based on measurable business impact.
* Facilitate cross-functional working sessions, resolve complex business problems, and personally drive critical initiatives to completion.
* Collaborate with colleagues in our Strategy and Transformation office in Europe, contributing to globally coordinated initiatives and sharing best practices across geographies.
* Present findings, recommendations, progress, and results to executive leadership and other key stakeholders
  

  

**KNOWLEDGE & SKILLS REQUIREMENTS**

* 10+ years of experience in transformation, strategy, operations, management consulting, or operational excellence, ideally within industrial, manufacturing, automation, or supply-chain environments.
* Demonstrated experience personally driving complex transformation initiatives from analysis through implementation, rather than primarily overseeing teams or programs.
* Proven track record of delivering measurable results, including revenue growth, margin expansion, cost reduction, productivity improvements, and other value-creation initiatives.
* Deep expertise in operational excellence, Lean / Six Sigma, and structured problem solving; Black Belt preferred.
* Experience with M&A integration, operating-model design, process optimization, and value-capture initiatives.
* Strong financial acumen, including P&L, EBIT, business cases, ROI, planning, and financial modeling.
* Strong analytical, strategic, and execution skills with the ability to move from high-level strategy into detailed implementation.
* Excellent executive communication and stakeholder-management skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority.
* MBA from a leading program and/or an engineering background strongly preferred.
* Experience with AI-enabled / digital transformation and agentic GTM.
* Warehouse/manufacturing automation domain knowledge, including WES/MES, aftermarket service, or commercial project controlling.
* ERP/SAP implementation or optimization experience.
* Global / multi-continent experience, particularly US and APAC.
* Experience working in a PE-backed or highly performance-driven industrial environment.

**PROFESSIONAL QUALITIES**

* Hands-on and action-oriented, with a willingness to personally dive into analysis, problem-solving, and execution.
* Highly analytical and intellectually curious, with the ability to simplify complex business challenges and identify practical solutions.
* Strong executive presence and communication skills, with the ability to influence and build credibility across all levels of the organization.
* Results-driven and accountable, with a strong focus on measurable business impact and value creation.
* Collaborative and adaptable, with the ability to navigate ambiguity and lead change without relying on direct authority.
  

  

**WORK CONDITIONS**

* Regular in-office collaboration with executive and cross-functional teams.
* Occasional domestic and international travel may be required to support business initiatives, operating locations, and global collaboration.
* Fast-paced, highly visible role requiring the ability to manage multiple strategic priorities and adapt as business needs evolve.
* Regular interaction with senior leadership and teams across functions, business units, and geographies.
  

  

**Why work for Storage Solutions – A Jungheinrich Company?**

At Storage Solutions, our greatest asset is our people. We have built a team of passionate intralogistics experts who collaborate and partner with distribution and fulfillment operations across North America and worldwide. We believe in providing tailored solutions for every square foot of an operation, and behind these solutions is a carefully selected team that shares our vision, culture, and core values.

We are committed to fostering a supportive and inclusive workplace where every team member can thrive. When you join us, you become part of a family that values your growth, well-being, and contributions. Together, we innovate, solve challenges, and celebrate successes.

existing_roles.description:
Here at Scout Motors, we're carrying forward the heritage of one of the most iconic American vehicles in history. A vehicle dating back to 1960. One that forged the path for future generations of rugged SUVs and trucks and will do so once again.

But Scout is more than just a brand, it's a legacy steeped in a culture of exploration, caretaking, and hard work.

The Scout brand is all about respect. Respect for the past and the future by taking an iconic American brand that hasn't been around for a while, electrifying it, digitizing it, and loading it with American innovation. Respect for communities by creating a company that stands for its people and its customers. Respect for both work and play, with vehicles that are equally at home at a camp site, a job site, or on a Tuesday commute. And respect for our customers by developing two powertrains that meet their requirements — an all-electric powertrain as well as the Harvester™ range extender powertrain which includes a built-in gas-powered generator with an estimated 500 miles of combined range.

At Scout Motors, we empower our talented, inclusive, and entrepreneurial teams to innovate. What makes a Scout employee? Someone who is a visionary and a leader, who seeks new paths and shares lessons learned. A knowledgeable doer who collaborates across the company to build better. A go-getter with unrivaled passion.

Join us at Scout Motors and be part of shaping the future of transportation. If you're ready to drive change and make history, apply now!

**Overview**

Scout Motors is seeking an Employee Operations Leader to build and lead the infrastructure that powers exceptional employee experiences at scale. This leader will own Scout's HR service delivery, systems ecosystem, and data governance — the operational backbone of the HR function.

As Scout grows, this role will be responsible for ensuring that every employee has seamless access to HR support, that our HR technology is configured and governed to support accurate data and reliable operations, and that our processes are disciplined, efficient, and continuously improving. This leader will partner closely with the Chief Human Resources Officer, HR centers of excellence, IT, Finance, and business leaders to build a high-performing HR operations function fit for a fast-scaling company.

#### **What you'll do**

Become part of an iconic brand that is set to revolutionize the electric pick-up truck & rugged SUV marketplace by achieving the following:

Leadership & Team Development

* Lead, develop, and coach a team spanning HR operations, HR systems architecture, and LMS administration.
* Set a clear vision for HR operations and inspire the team to deliver consistent, high-quality service to employees and people leaders.
* Create a culture of continuous improvement, accountability, and operational excellence within the team.
* Partner with the CHRO and HR leadership team to align operational priorities with the broader HR strategy.
* Champion inclusion, collaboration, and Scout's cultural values within the team and across the function.

HR Service Delivery & Operations

* Oversee Scout's HR service delivery model including Tier 0 self-service tools with the use of AI, resources, knowledge bases, and exception-handling protocols.
* Ensure employees and managers have timely, accurate access to HR support and information.
* Set and monitor SLAs, service metrics, and quality standards for HR operations.
* Lead continuous improvement of service delivery processes to improve the employee and people leader experience, with heavy focus on ensuring HR data quality and enabling self service capabilities.
* Manage escalation pathways for complex or sensitive HR inquiries, ensuring consistent and compliant resolution.

HR Systems & Technology

* Own Scout's HR technology ecosystem, including HRIS, LMS, ATS, and potential future talent marketplace platforms.
* Partner with IT, vendors, and HR centers of excellence to evaluate, implement, and optimize HR technologies.
* In collaboration with IT and potentially other vendors, establish agentic AI as the first level of engagement (Tier 0) for employees and people leaders to respond routine inquiries
* Where necessary, establish a workflow for inquiries that require greater consideration and action from HR Partners or other Subject Matter Experts.
* Drive system governance including configuration decisions, access management, and platform roadmap planning.
* Ensure integrations between HR systems are stable, accurate, and aligned with business needs.
* Stay current on HR technology trends and proactively identify opportunities to modernize or streamline the HR tech stack.

Data, Reporting & Governance

* Own Scout's HR data strategy, reporting infrastructure, and workforce analytics capabilities.
* Establish data governance frameworks, standards, and audit processes that ensure data quality, accuracy, and compliance.
* Partner with Finance, Legal, and business stakeholders to deliver workforce reporting and insights that inform people and organizational decisions.
* Build dashboards and reporting tools that give leaders visibility into the health and performance of the workforce.

**Location & Travel Expectations**:

* This role will be based out of the **Scout Motors corporate headquarters in Charlotte, NC**.
* This role requires 4 days per week in the office, with regular in-person meetings and events.
* **Travel**: Domestic and minimal international travel may be required as business needs evolve. Valid driver's license required. Passport required

#### **What you'll bring**

We expect all Scout employees to have integrity, curiosity, resourcefulness, and strive to exhibit a positive attitude, as well as a growth mindset. You'll be comfortable with change and flexible in a fast-paced, high-growth environment. You'll take a collaborative approach to achieve ambitious goals. Here's what else you'll bring:

* Bachelor's degree required; Master's degree, MBA, or advanced HR-related degree preferred.
* 12+ years of progressive HR experience with significant experience in HR operations, HRIS, or shared services leadership.
* Demonstrated experience managing and optimizing HR technology platforms such as HRIS, ATS, and LMS systems.
* Experience building or leading HR shared services or operations functions in high-growth or transformational environments.
* Strong analytical skills and comfort with HR data, metrics, reporting, and business intelligence tools.
* Experience managing cro$180,000.00 - $220,000.00s-functional projects and leading teams through technology implementations or process change.
* Exceptional organizational, communication, and stakeholder management skills.
* Ability to balance strategic vision with hands-on operational execution.
* Demonstrated grit, curiosity, and resourcefulness in navigating ambiguity, solving complex problems, and turning obstacles into practical, scalable solutions.
* High integrity, sound judgment, and a commitment to inclusion, fairness, and respect.
* Experience in startup, scaling, automotive, or manufacturing environments is strongly preferred.

#### **What you'll gain**

The benefits of joining Scout include the chance to build products and a company from the ground up. This is a chance to create something new and lasting – with an iconic brand at its foundation. In addition, Scout provides competitive compensation and benefits to support your physical, mental, and financial wellbeing. Program specifics are detailed in company policies and employee benefit guides, select highlights:

* Competitive insurance including:
  + Medical, dental, vision and income protection plans
* 401(k) program with:
  + An employer match and immediate vesting
* Generous Paid Time Off including:
  + 20 days planned PTO, as accrued
  + 40 hours of unplanned PTO and 14 company or floating holidays, annually
  + Up to 16 weeks of paid parental leave for biological and adoptive parents of all genders
  + Paid leave for circumstances related to bereavement, jury duty, voting time, or military leave
* Corporate Vehicle Program with:
  + Eligibility for 1 assigned vehicle
  + A mobility stipend

#### **Pay Transparency**

This is a full-time, exempt position eligible to receive a base salary and to participate in an annual performance bonus program. Final salary offered will be determined based on factors including but not limited to the candidate's skills and experience. The annual performance bonus program is preset and not candidate dependent.

Initial base salary range = $180,000.00 - $220,000.00

Internal leveling code: M6

**Notice to applicants:**

* To be considered for career opportunities at Scout Motors, applicants must be 18 years of age or older.
* Residing in **San Francisco**: *Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.*
* Residing in **Los Angeles**: *Scout Motors will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with the Los Angeles Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance.*
* Residing in **New York City**: *This role is not eligible for remote work in New York City.*

  

**Equal Opportunity**

Scout Motors is committed to employing a diverse workforce and is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, veteran status, disability, pregnancy, or any other characteristics protected by law. Scout Motors is committed to compliance with all applicable fair employment practice laws. If you require reasonable accommodation to complete a job application, pre-employment testing, or a job interview or to otherwise participate in the hiring process, please contact ScoutAccommodations@scoutmotors.com.

**Summit Polymers is a leading, global supplier of automotive interior systems including consoles, door panels, and instrument panels. With over 50 years serving the industry, we deliver engineering and product excellence to our customers, on time, in budget, with the latest innovations.**
JOIN A TEAM WHERE YOU’LL BE CHALLENGED AND valued.
  
  
A career with Summit Polymers means working with smart people in a culture that thrives on challenging, meaningful work. At Summit, we look for growth potential with every hire. We don’t just fill seats, we set people on career paths. We’re always on the lookout for smart people who are committed to continuous improvement, customer service and quality.
  
  
**Job Description**
**JOB TITLE:**
Director, Corporate Quality
**FLSA STATUS:**
Exempt
  
  
**REPORTS TO:**
Regional Director of Manufacturing (Corporate)
  
  
**Summary**
This management position is responsible for developing, implementing and continually improving the company’s standardized manufacturing quality systems globally. The Director, Corporate Quality works collaboratively with plant quality managers, general managers and other company resources to achieve world class quality performance as measured by customer quality scorecards. The Director, Corporate Quality interfaces with key customer personnel to build customer confidence in Summit Polymers, ensure Summit Polymers meets customer expectations and requirements, and to resolve significant customer quality concerns.
  
  
**Responsibilities And Duties**
Is responsible for the following major tasks:
  
  

* Exhibits positive leadership and acts with highest levels of integrity and ethics
* Champions corporate wide manufacturing quality system standardization

+ Leads and collaborates with plant quality managers, general managers and RDMs to determine best practices and develop standardized quality system and procedures applicable to all manufacturing facilities
+ Administers, trains, and communicates the company’s standardized quality system and procedures to ensure they are effectively implemented and maintained throughout the company
+ Performs plant quality system standards compliance audits and leads follow up action plan reviews with each plant
+ Lead continuous improvement of quality systems

* Champions overall quality scorecard performance for all customers

+ Develops deep knowledge of every customer quality scorecard
+ Leads specific customer scorecard training for plant quality managers, materials managers and general managers to ensure these leaders understand scoring methodology and act to ensure scorecard success
+ Monitors customer scorecard methodology and scoring changes, and ensures corporate procedures, metrics and personnel proactively adapt to changes to ensure customer scorecard success
+ Engages with other functional departments to ensure all aspects of customer scorecards are understood and actions are taken to ensure scorecard success (examples Sales – cost reductions, materials – minority sourcing)
+ Assists in developing internal performance metrics that support successful customer scorecard results

* Interfaces with key customer personnel & engages customer quality events

+ Develops constructive relationships with key customer contacts
+ Builds customer’s confidence in SPI’s performance, capabilities, systems, and integrity
+ Represents the company at customer “quality roundtable” events
+ Reviews customer quality system requirements and specifications and ensure they are effectively communicated and implemented at all levels of the organization

* Engages in significant customer quality concerns and warranty issues

+ Participates in problem solving and customer response preparation for significant customer quality issues
+ Represents the company at critical customer quality concern reviews, leading company response and negotiation to achieve successful resolution
+ Acts as point of contact for customer warranty concerns and engages plant and engineering resources to solve warranty concerns

* Provides quality expertise as a corporate resource

+ Champions Practical Problem Solving activities across the company, including improving effectiveness of management team leadership of the process
+ Key leader for development, update, training and compliance to corporate IATF-16949 compliant systems and procedures
+ Supports new business initiatives and projects with data, metrics, support plans, and technical expertise as related to quality
+ Provide support in developing and performing training plans for quality managers and quality engineers at manufacturing plants
+ Provides additional support at manufacturing plants as needed

* Other tasks and duties as assigned

**Education And Experience**

* 4-year college degree in technical or management field preferred
* 5 years’ experience in role of Quality Manager at automotive supplier preferred

**Skills And Abilities**

* Broad knowledge of quality systems and management practices in automotive plastics manufacturing operations
* Expertise in major automotive OEM quality systems; Ford Q1, GM BIQS, FCA, Nissan, VW, BMW, and Toyota
* Expert problem solving skills utilizing root cause based methods; Practical Problem Solving (PPS), 8D, and 5 why methodology
* Must be able to gather and analyze information easily and make appropriate decisions.
* Outstanding leadership, team building, coaching and decision making abilities
* Highly energetic, confident, and assertive with the ability to lead and motivate others
* Must have excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills
* A minimum score of 50 on the Wonderlic Select Assessment (Traditional score of 28 on the cognitive portion).

**Travel Requirements**
This position typically does require approximately 18 weeks per year of travel to Summit Polymers Manufacturing Sites.
  
  
**DISCLAIMER**
The information contained in this job description is not intended to be an all-inclusive list of the duties and responsibilities of the job, nor are they intended to be an all-inclusive list of the skills and abilities required to do the job. Management may, at its discretion, assign or reassign duties and responsibilities to this job at any time. Agreement to complete all post-hire required training.

protected_roles.description:
As the
**Director of Quality**
, you will lead the quality strategy and continuous improvement efforts across all Bison manufacturing sites. You will be responsible for ensuring that the products meet or exceed customer expectations, industry standards, and regulatory requirements while driving overall quality performance and fostering a culture of continuous improvement. You will work closely with cross-functional teams to establish and maintain effective quality systems, drive process improvements, and ensure compliance with industry certifications.
  
  
This position can be based at either our
**Whitsett, NC**
or
**Reynosa, MX**
facility.
  
  
**What You Will Do**
  
  

* Leadership & Strategy

+ Develop and execute a strategic quality plan in alignment with business unit goals.
+ Lead, mentor, and develop a team of quality professionals across two locations, ensuring consistency in processes and objectives.
+ Champion a culture of quality, accountability, and continuous improvement.

* Quality Management Systems (QMS)

+ Oversee the implementation, maintenance, and improvement of the QAD Elements QMS and other relevant Quality Management Systems at both locations. Ensure compliance with customer, regulatory, and industry-specific quality standards (e.g., FDA, ISO, AS9100, etc.).
+ Monitor and evaluate the effectiveness of quality management systems and propose enhancements to improve overall performance.

* Process & Product Quality

+ Collaborate with sales, operations, engineering, and supply chain teams to identify drive resolution of quality issues, ensuring process and product integrity.
+ Support root cause analysis and drive corrective and preventive actions (CAPA) for internal and external quality issues.
+ Oversee first article inspections, process capability studies, and validation/qualification activities to ensure robust manufacturing processes.

* Continuous Improvement

+ Lead Lean Six Sigma or other continuous improvement initiatives aimed at reducing defects, enhancing efficiency, and improving overall quality.
+ Implement data-driven decision-making tools (e.g., SPC, FMEA, Control Plans) to monitor and improve process capabilities.
+ Facilitate cross-functional value stream mapping sessions and quality workshops to drive process improvements.

* Customer & Supplier Relations

+ Serve as the main point of contact for customer quality issues, audits, and feedback, ensuring timely and effective resolution.
+ Oversee supplier quality management, including audits, performance monitoring, and supplier development initiatives.

* Metrics & Reporting

+ Establish and track key performance indicators (KPIs) related to quality performance, including scrap/rework, defect rates, customer complaints, and audit findings.
+ Regularly report quality performance metrics to senior leadership, highlighting trends and recommending corrective actions.

* Regulatory Compliance & Audits

+ Lead internal and external audits, ensuring the sites comply with relevant standards and certifications.
+ Ensure the manufacturing facilities are audit-ready at all times and coordinate responses to audit findings.

**What We Are Looking For**

* Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field. Master’s degree preferred.
* 10+ years of progressive experience in quality management within a manufacturing environment, with at least 5 years in a leadership role.
* Demonstrated experience with quality management systems (ISO 9001, AS9100, FDA, or equivalent) and continuous improvement methodologies (Lean, Six Sigma).
* Demonstrated ability and willingness to use AI tools to improve productivity, decision-making, work quality, and to reduce costs. The successful candidate must be able to identify appropriate AI use cases and critically evaluate AI-generated outputs.
* Proven track record of driving quality improvements across multi-site operations.
* Ability to travel as needed to the BU manufacturing sites (up to 30%)
* Strong leadership and team-building skills.
* Excellent analytical and problem-solving abilities.
* Ability to communicate effectively with all levels of the organization.
* Proficiency in quality tools such as SPC, FMEA, 8D, and Root Cause Analysis.

**Compensation**
Employee Type: Salaried
  
  
Currency: USD
  
  
Salary Minimum: 135,000
  
  
Salary Maximum: 185,000
  
  
Incentive: Yes
  
  
Disclaimer: Where a specific pay range is noted, it is a good faith estimate at the time of this posting. The actual salary offered will be based on experience, skills, qualifications, market / business considerations, and geographic location.

****Job Description:****
**Are you ready to steer quality operations for a global leader in vertical flight?**
Airbus Helicopters is seeking a visionary, results-oriented
**Site Quality Director**
to lead our site-level Quality Management System (QMS) and daily operational integrity. Reporting directly to the VP of Quality, you will serve as the operational anchor for aviation safety, manufacturing excellence, and regulatory compliance across FAA, EASA, TCCA, and AS9100 standards.
  
  
In this high-visibility leadership role, you will direct a team of quality professionals across logistics, assembly, component repair, and final conformity. We are looking for a strategic change-maker who can embed a "First Time Right" mindset, harmonize site practices with global Airbus standards, and bridge the gap between engineering, regulatory bodies, and frontline operations.
  
  
**Your working environment:**
On the eastern border of Mississippi you’ll find Columbus, home to our Helicopter manufacturing and assembly lines and Center of Excellence for the entire North America region. It’s here that we produce the UH-72A Lakota Helicopters for the U.S. Army in addition to the H-125 aircraft for civil and commercial customers.
  
  
**How we care for you:**

* Financial Rewards: Competitive base salary, incentive compensation which may include profit sharing schemes, retirement savings plan and the ability to participate in an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (“ESOP”)
* Work/Life Balance: Paid time off including personal time, holidays and a generous paid parental leave program.
* Health & Welfare: Comprehensive insurance coverage including medical (traditional and high-deductible health plans), prescription, dental, vision, life, disability, Employee Assistance Plan (“EAP”) and other supplemental benefit coverages.
* Individual Development: Upskilling and development opportunities through our global Leadership University, including unlimited access to 10,000+ e-learning courses focusing on ways to develop your employability, certifications, career path as well as the opportunity to participate in accelerated development programmes and both national and international mobility.

**Your Challenges:**

* Sustain Regulatory & Quality Certifications: Maintain, uphold, and expand site compliance for FAA, EASA, and TCCA repair station and production certificates, certified personnel, and AS9100 QMS credentials.
* Drive Executive QMS Governance: Administer the site Quality Management System, collaborating directly with the Executive Committee to embed strategic quality objectives into the business planning cycle.
* Standardize Operational Inspections: Supervise and enforce rigorous inspection standards across supply chain, logistics, receiving, in-process assembly, quality gates, and final aircraft conformity for components, aerostructures, and rotorcraft.
* Mitigate Quality Escapes & Risk: Identify and eliminate operational and airworthiness risks to safeguard customer flight safety, business continuity, delivery schedules, and operating costs.
* Lead and Develop Personnel: Directly manage, mentor, and evaluate a team of 3-5 exempt supervisors/engineers and 10-25 non-exempt inspectors, directing career progression, staffing, and technical competence.
* Establish & Track SQCDP KPIs: Implement robust enterprise metrics tracking Safety, Quality, Cost, Delivery, and People (SQCDP) to systematically capture non-conformances, process capability, and customer complaints.
* Manage Financials & Quality Budget: Direct departmental budgeting, manage financial forecasts, analyze cost variances, and allocate capital for advanced measurement tools, calibration, and ergonomic work environments.
* Execute Root Cause & Corrective Action (RCCA): Drive practical problem solving (PPS), Plan-Do-Check-Act (PDCA), and structured RCCA workflows to resolve manufacturing anomalies and prevent recurrence.
* Harmonize Global Airbus Standards: Coordinate with international Airbus Helicopters facilities to standardize quality procedures, digital architectures, and enterprise systems (including SAP, MES, and non-conformance portals).
* Champion Safety and "First Time Right" Culture: Spearhead a proactive, psychological safety culture anchored by "First Time Right" execution and a robust "Speak Up / Listen Up" mindset across all shifts and departments.
* Direct Internal & External Audits: Lead preparation, execution, and reporting for internal, regulatory (FAA/EASA/TCCA), and customer audits, ensuring all corrective action milestones are closed transparently.
* Collaborate on Design & New Product Introduction (NPI): Partner with design engineering and certification teams to support new product development, configuration integrity, obsolescence management, and manufacturing build cycles.
* Reduce Cost of Non-Quality (CoNQ): Lead enterprise continuous improvement, Lean, and Kaizen initiatives to eliminate scrap, minimize rework, reduce the Cost of Non-Quality, and improve delivery reliability.
* Optimize Workload & Production Flow: Coordinate with operations and program management to balance inspection staffing and shift priorities against critical flightline and customer delivery schedules.
* Oversee Technical Training & Qualifications: Build and finance comprehensive onboarding and recurrent training programs covering aviation safety, specialized processes (NDI, composites, dynamic components), and regulatory requirements.

**Your Boarding Pass:**

* Must possess a Bachelor’s Degree in Aerospace/Aviation/Industrial Engineer/Engineering related field or equivalent experience (4 years)
* Have ten (10) + years of Aerospace/Aviation Industry, Military or Quality experience and three (3) + years in a Leadership role, Civilian and/or Military
* Able to support functions in multiple areas such as repair station, manufacturing, composites, electrical/avionics Backshop, warehousing/logistics, dynamic component repair, blades and tail boom
* Knowledge of Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Regulations 14 CFR Parts 21, 43 and 145 in addition the related sections for Transport Canada and EASA
* Knowledge of AS9100 Quality Requirements and Systems
* Knowledge of aircraft design, maintenance, and manufacturing processes and build cycles
* Microsoft Office Suite (Excel, PowerPoint, Word and Access), Onbase, Orion eTechPub, Adobe Acrobat , SAP, Smartsheet, G Suite. OCE/ARAS/Bflow T.I.P.I.

**Preferred Education/Skills:**

* Master’s Degree as described above
* 12 years of Aerospace/Aviation Industry, Military or Quality experience and 3 years in a Leadership role Civilian and/or Military
* A&P License
* ASQ or CMQ certified

**Travel Required:**

* 15% Domestic and International

**Citizenship:**

* Must be a US Person under ITAR definition (U.S. Citizen, green card holder or person covered under our existing ITAR license)

**Physical Requirements:**

* Onsite or remote: 100% in Columbus, MS unless traveling
* Vision: able to see and read computer screens and other electronic equipment with screens, able to read documents, reports and engineering drawings daily. Must have correctable near and far vision if applicable.
* Hearing: able to hear to participate in conversations in person and via teleconference or phone and to hear sounds on the production floor including safety warnings or alarms. Daily
* Speaking: able to speak in conversations and meetings, deliver information and participate in communications. Daily
* Equipment Operation (personal computer, telephone, copies, fax machine, and related office equipment and using electronic identification card to enter building floors and internal doors): able to operate most office and personal electronic equipment and some tools including production tools .
* Carrying: able to carry documents, tools, drawings, electronic equipment up to 30lbs/14kgs. Daily
* Lifting: able to lift documents, tools, drawings, electronic equipment up to 30lbs/14kgs. Daily
* Pushing / Pulling: able to push and pull small office furniture and some equipment and tools. Daily
* Sitting: able to sit for long periods of time in meetings, working on the computer. Several times a week
* Squatting / Kneeling: able to squat or kneel to retrieve or replace items stored on low shelving. Daily
* Standing: able to stand for discussions in offices or on the production floor. Daily
* Travel: able to travel independently and at short notice. 15% or less yearly
* Walking (include routine walking such as to a shared printer to retrieve documents): able to walk through office and production areas including uneven surfaces. Daily
* Personal Protective Equipment required: Required PPE includes, but is not limited to, Safety Shoes, Safety Glasses, Hearing Protection, Respirators/Masks, and/or Protective Gloves as required by site and/or customer site
* Administrative position only PPE required: Steel-toed shoes are required for all shop floor visits, appropriate hearing/eye protection may also be required when visiting the shop floor.

**Overview**
Resonetics is a global leader in advanced engineering, prototyping, product development, and micro manufacturing, driving innovation in the medical device industry. With rapid expansion across all our locations, we continue to push the boundaries of technology while fostering a dynamic, employee-centered culture. Our commitment to excellence and continuous improvement makes Resonetics an exciting place for professionals passionate about shaping the future of micro-manufacturing and being part of something bigger
  
  
The Quality Director plays a pivotal role in leading and strengthening operational quality and quality compliance within a large-scale contract manufacturing facility. Responsible for both Product Quality and Quality Management System (QMS) compliance, this leader ensures quality operations within the manufacturing environment consistently meet customer, regulatory, and business expectations.
  
  
This individual combines strategic vision with hands-on operational quality leadership, ensuring Resonetics delivers world-class quality in a fast-paced, highly regulated medical device manufacturing environment. The role demands proven experience within manufacturing operations, deep expertise in ISO 13485 and 21 CFR Part 820, mastery of advanced quality assurance techniques, and the ability to align and elevate quality performance across multiple value streams.
  
  
Join Resonetics and be part of a team that’s redefining medical device manufacturing. If you’re passionate about innovation and thrive in a fast-paced environment, we’d love to hear from you.
  
  
**Responsibilities**
**Operational Quality Leadership**

* Own and lead all aspects of manufacturing quality performance, ensuring operational processes deliver consistent, compliant, and high-yield outcomes.
* Partner closely with Operations leadership to embed quality into daily production activities and drive problem-solving directly on the manufacturing floor.
* Implement and oversee statistical process control (SPC), process capability, and other data-driven tools to ensure process stability and continuous improvement.
* Monitor and manage critical quality metrics, taking immediate action to address gaps and prevent recurrence of issues.
* Oversee validation strategies (IQ/OQ/PQ) for manufacturing processes and equipment, ensuring robustness and compliance.
* Provide quality leadership in New Product Introduction (NPI), ensuring robust process validation, risk management, and seamless transition from development into full-scale manufacturing.

**Quality Systems & Compliance**

* Ensure the ISO-certified QMS is operationally effective within manufacturing sites and continuously improved to support business growth.
* Maintain full compliance with ISO 13485, 21 CFR Part 820, and other relevant standards through proactive system management and audit readiness.

**Continuous Improvement & Problem Solving**

* Lead root cause investigations and corrective actions for complex production challenges.
* Drive Lean and Six Sigma initiatives that enhance manufacturing efficiency while strengthening compliance and product quality.
* Share best practices across sites to ensure standardization and scalability of quality improvements.

**Customer & Supplier Interface**

* Serve as the primary quality leader for high-visibility customers, ensuring confidence in Resonetics’ ability to deliver consistently high-quality products.
* Lead the supplier quality program, ensuring raw materials and outsourced processes meet stringent requirements to support operational excellence.

**Team Leadership & Development**

* Build and mentor a strong quality team embedded within the manufacturing organization.
* Provide training in advanced quality tools (Gage R&R, SPC, pFMEA, Risk Analysis, Validation, Root Cause Analysis, CAPA) to elevate operational capability.
* Foster a culture of quality culture and ownership on the production floor, engaging all levels of the workforce.

**Required Qualifications**

* Minimum 7 years’ experience in a Medical Device Quality Management role.
* Lean and/or Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt
* Demonstrated background in an ISO 13485 and 21 CFR 820 quality management system.
* Strong communication skills (verbal and writing)
* BS degree in a management or engineering discipline
* Experience hosting FDA inspections and ISO audits

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Prior experience in a technical, regulated environment.
* Experience with finished medical device assembly and oversight of sterilization
* Experience with Quality Management Software (eQMS) and ERP systems
* Certified Quality Auditor

**Physical Demands**

* Light office work, approximately 25%+ travel

**Compensation**
The compensation for this role is competitive and will be based on experience and qualifications. The anticipated range is $144,000.00 - $222,000.00.
  
  
For temp, temp-to-hire, and regular full-time positions, our company policy is that we are unable to provide visa sponsorship. Candidates must already be legally authorized to work in the United States without the need for sponsorship now or in the future.

The Director of Process Engineering is responsible for leading the development, optimization, and scale-up of manufacturing processes to support Mott Corporation's growth across Semiconductor, Aerospace & Defense, and Industrial markets. This role drives process stability, improves yield and cost performance, and ensures successful industrialization of new products.

* Efficient, scalable production for Industrial markets

* Yield and First Pass Yield (FPY) improvement

* Scrap and rework reduction programs
* Lead root cause analysis and structured problem-solving for manufacturing and quality issues
* Standardize and document processes, work instructions, and best practices

* Collaborate across functions to accelerate time-to-market for new programs

* Lead Lean and Six Sigma initiatives to improve productivity and reduce cost

First Pass Yield targets across Semiconductor, A&D, and Industrial lines

Throughput improvements and bottleneck elimination

**Position Overview: Director of Engineering – Enrichment Operations**

Engineering Leadership & Organization

Systems Engineering (SE)

Manufacturing Excellence & DFx
  
  

* Deliver engineering solutions capable of automotive‑pace production with aerospace‑grade quality.
* Drive design for manufacturability, assembly, quality, cost, and industrialization (DFM/DFA/DFQ/DFC).

Quality, Safety & Compliance
  
  

* Ensure all engineering designs and processes meet nuclear regulatory, DOE, safety, and BWXT quality requirements.
* Embed compliance gates, audit readiness, and pre‑release checks throughout development.

Program Controls & Schedule
  
  

* Partner with Business Operations and Program Controls to maintain a resource‑loaded critical path schedule.
* Support earned value management (EVM) discipline and weekly KPI reviews (SPI/CPI, cost variance, schedule adherence).

Supply Chain & Technical Readiness
  
  

* Define technical acceptance criteria for supplier parts, processes, tooling, and special manufacturing steps.
* Support supplier onboarding speed, delivery performance, and technical readiness to protect schedule-critical components.

Cross-Functional Collaboration
  
  

* Work closely with CMDF (prototype/pilot operations), CMF (full-rate industrialization), the CTO/Technology organization, and Operations.

**Preferred Qualifications**

**Application Close Date**
Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis until the requisition is closed.
  
  
At Blue Origin, we envision millions of people living and working in space for the benefit of Earth. We’re working to develop reusable, safe, and low-cost space vehicles and systems within a culture of safety, collaboration, and inclusion. Join our team of problem solvers as we add new chapters to the history of spaceflight!
  
  
This role is part of Blue Origin Operations, which is comprised of Integrated Supply Chain, Test Operations, Safety, Quality, and Mission Assurance. This includes Manufacturing and Supply Chain support across all Blue Origin facilities.
  
  
We are a team of collaborators, doers, and problem-solvers who are relentlessly committed to a culture of safety. This position will directly impact the history of space exploration and will require your commitment and detailed attention towards safe and repeatable spaceflight. Join us in lowering the cost of access to space and enabling Blue Origin's vision of millions of people living and working in space to benefit Earth.
  
  
As part of a hardworking, passionate, and accomplished team of experts, you will own the financial and operational execution for our BE-4 Engines high-volume fabrication teams at the Explorer Facility in Huntsville, Alabama. You will lead a skilled, interdisciplinary team responsible for Machining including 5-axis machining at scale, lathe, and related metal-cutting operations, Fluids Systems Fabrication (Tube and Weld Shops with both robotic and manual welding, Subassemblies, Precision Cleaning, and Pressure Vessels), Avionics Fabrication (Avionics Processing and Cable Harnesses), Coatings, and Thermal Protection Systems (TPS) in support of orbital launch vehicle engine production. This is a hands-on leadership role that demands deep fabrication-process expertise and the ability to communicate vision and strategy while driving the tactical application of cost-effective practices and key deliverables. Success depends on strong cross-functional leadership and collaboration across quality, engineering, supply chain, and production. You will report directly to the Sr. Director of Operations for BE-4 Engines at the Explorer Facility.
  
  
We are looking for someone to apply their leadership skills, technical expertise, and unwavering commitment to safety and quality to positively impact safe human spaceflight. Passion for our mission and vision is required!
  
  
**Responsibilities**

* Lead high-volume manufacturing operations encompassing quality, engineering, supply chain, and production across all fabrication areas and work centers at the Explorer Facility in Huntsville.
* Direct initiatives and strategies that deliver cost-effective, high-quality operational performance in support of orbital launch vehicle development for payload and human spaceflight.
* Implement methods to increase production efficiency and productivity, including factory flow optimization, higher throughput within existing floor space, improved first-pass yield, increased output, accelerated learning curves, and supplier on-time delivery.
* Propagate key operational learnings and best practices to drive continuous improvement across Explorer Facility operations and the broader Blue Origin enterprise.
* Champion safety and first-time quality across all functions while actively growing and developing your team at all levels.
* Analyze processes and operations at both micro and macro levels, implementing high-impact improvements for safety and quality that reduce unit cost and accelerate throughput.
* Oversee the development and implementation of data-driven systems with a lean approach, maintaining a sharp focus on delivering measurable results.
* Leverage Blue Origin's Leadership Principles to cultivate a trusting, learning culture through continuous feedback, coaching, and robust development opportunities — fostering a "One Team Mindset" across the Huntsville site and partner organizations.

**Basic Qualifications**

* Proven track record of building or transforming successful production organizations and leading large-scale change management initiatives that shape culture, define tools and processes, and improve competencies.
* Bachelor's degree (BA/BS) or equivalent experience with an emphasis in Operations Management or Manufacturing Engineering, with a history of progressive responsibility.
* 10+ years of manufacturing leadership experience.
* Prior experience in a Factory or Plant leadership role required.
* Strong working knowledge and applied experience in Lean Manufacturing and Six Sigma methodologies.
* Experience leading, growing, and developing large teams within a multi-business unit, integrated supply chain organization.
* Advanced knowledge in designing and building manufacturing, production, assembly, procurement, and logistics systems in a low-volume, high-complexity environment.
* Strong business acumen with demonstrated experience challenging the status quo, driving change, and motivating individuals to develop and implement innovative approaches.
* Proven success in hiring and developing high-performing teams with diverse skill sets.
* Ability to create and manage work cell standard work and effectively track deviations from established standards.
* Experience managing capital improvements and facility layout planning.
* Highly effective verbal and written communication skills with a strong emphasis on teamwork and internal/external customer satisfaction.
* A world-class attitude toward mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
* Ability to maintain positive, professional relationships and actively contribute to a culture of trust, respect, inclusion, and integrity.
* Must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.

**Desired Qualifications**

* 15+ years of manufacturing experience in aerospace industries such as launch vehicles, aircraft, or rotorcraft.
* Master's degree in Engineering, Operations, or Business.
* Experience across multiple manufacturing processes and technologies, including metal machining, composites, aerostructures, welding, and harness fabrication.
* Earned Value Management (EVM) experience.
* Familiarity with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) systems.

**Culture Statement**
Don’t meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Blue Origin, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
  
  
**Export Control Regulations**
Applicants for employment at Blue Origin must be a U.S. citizen or national, U.S. permanent resident (i.e. current Green Card holder), or lawfully admitted into the U.S. as a refugee or granted asylum.
  
  
**Background Check**

* Required for all positions: Blue’s Standard Background Check
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Defense Biometric Identification System (DBIDS) background check if at any time the role requires one to be on a military installation
* Required for Certain Job Profiles: Drivers who operate Commercial Motor Vehicles with a Gross Vehicle Weight (GVW), Gross Vehicle Weight Rating (GVWR) or combination of power unit and trailer that meets or exceeds 10,001 lbs. and/or transports placardable amounts of hazardous materials by ground in any vehicle on a public road while in commerce, may be subject to additional Federal Motor Carrier Safety Regulations including: Driver Qualification Files, Medical Certification (obtained before onboarding), Road Test, Hours of Service, Drug and Alcohol Testing, vehicle inspection requirements, CDL requirements (if applicable) and hazardous materials transportation/shipping training.
* Required for certain Job Profiles: Ability to obtain and maintain Merchant Mariner Credential, which includes pre-employment and random drug testing as well as DOT physical

**Benefits**

* Benefits include: Medical, dental, vision, basic and supplemental life insurance, paid parental leave, short and long-term disability, 401(k) with a company match of up to 5%, and an Education Support Program.
* Stock Options for all regular employees (working at least 20 hours/week)

* Dependent on role type and job level, employees may be eligible for benefits and bonuses based on the company's intent to reward individual contributions and enable them to share in the company's results, or other factors at the company's sole discretion. Bonus amounts and eligibility are not guaranteed and subject to change and cancellation. Please check with your recruiter for more details.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**
Blue Origin is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action Employer and is committed to attracting, retaining, and developing a highly qualified and dedicated work force. Blue Origin hires and promotes people on the basis of their qualifications, performance, and abilities. We support the establishment and maintenance of a workplace that fosters trust, equality, and teamwork. We provide all qualified applicants for employment and employees with equal opportunities for hire, promotion, and other terms and conditions of employment, regardless of their race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin/ethnicity, age, physical or mental disability, genetic factors, military/veteran status, or any other status or characteristic protected by federal, state, and/or local law. Blue Origin will consider for employment qualified applicants with criminal histories in a manner consistent with applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the Washington Fair Chance Act, the California Fair Chance Act, the Los Angeles Fair Chance in Hiring Ordinance, and other applicable laws. For more information on “Know Your Rights,” please see here.
  
  
**Affirmative Action and Disability Accommodation**
Applicants wishing to receive information on Blue Origin’s Affirmative Action Plans, or applicants requiring a reasonable accommodation in order to participate in the application and/or interview process, please contact us at EEOCompliance@blueorigin.com. protected_roles.title: Senior Manager, DNA Manufacturing Operations & Integration
protected_roles.description:
**The Role**
Joining Moderna means advancing mRNA science to transform medicine. Work with exceptional global teams on a broad pipeline and build a career that makes a real difference for patients.
  
  
Moderna is strengthening its presence in Norwood, Massachusetts, a cornerstone of our manufacturing and operational excellence. Our Norwood campus translates mRNA science into scalable impact, supporting the global delivery of our medicines. We welcome talent ready to drive innovation and make a meaningful difference for patients worldwide.
  
  
This is an opportunity to lead at the intersection of DNA Manufacturing, Cell Bank operations, Operational Excellence, technology transfer, quality, digital capability, and manufacturing performance, helping translate complex technical and business priorities into reliable execution.
  
  
You will lead a highly capable team while owning the continuous improvement agenda for DNA Manufacturing, using operational data, structured problem solving, and cross-functional leadership to identify risks, unlock capacity, strengthen processes, and deliver sustainable improvements.
  
  
As a member of the DNA Leadership Team, you will influence priorities beyond your immediate function, solve complex and ambiguous challenges across organizational boundaries, and help build the manufacturing capabilities, culture, and digital ways of working needed for the next stage of Moderna’s operations.
  
  
**Here’s What You’ll Do**

* Lead, develop, and coach a team of Specialists and Senior Specialists with broad expertise across DNA and Cell Bank manufacturing processes, building a highly capable and adaptable team that can address evolving operational priorities.
* Own and continuously improve the DNA Manufacturing continuous improvement and Operational Excellence program, including the identification, prioritization, execution, and benefits realization of improvement opportunities.
* Lead complex, cross-functional initiatives spanning DNA Manufacturing and partner organizations, establishing clear objectives, governance, execution plans, decision-making mechanisms, and accountability for delivery.
* Own the strategy and execution of manufacturing change controls associated with area improvements, ensuring changes are effectively planned, assessed, implemented, embedded, and sustained within manufacturing operations.
* Provide manufacturing leadership and execution support for technology transfers, serving as the Manufacturing representative, coordinating manufacturing readiness activities, and providing project management across cross-functional teams to enable successful transfer and execution.
* Lead the use of operational data, performance indicators, manufacturing trends, and operational insights to proactively identify emerging risks, improvement opportunities, capacity constraints, and priorities for DNA Operations.
* Establish and continuously evolve effective operational performance management mechanisms, including dashboards, routine performance reviews, action tracking, and escalation processes for emerging issues.
* Serve as a GMP leader and manufacturing subject matter expert, providing support for investigations, operational events, risk assessments, change implementation, and other quality system activities as required.
* Partner closely with Manufacturing Science & Technology (MSAT), Quality Assurance, Supply Chain, Digital, CMC Development, Planning, and other stakeholders to integrate technical, quality, supply, and business priorities into effective manufacturing execution.
* Support the organization’s ongoing state of inspection readiness, ensuring the team, processes, documentation, change activity, and improvements within the role’s scope are prepared to effectively support regulatory inspections.
* Build organizational capability in continuous improvement, structured problem solving, project execution, data-driven decision making, and change management, strengthening the organization’s ability to respond effectively to evolving manufacturing needs.
* Serve as a member of the DNA Leadership Team, contributing to strategy, organizational priorities, operational performance, workforce engagement, and the resolution of issues affecting the broader DNA Operations organization.
* Foster a positive, collaborative, accountable, and inclusive working culture across DNA Manufacturing, acting as a visible leader and role model while supporting the overall performance and well-being of the organization.
* Act as a trusted advisor and problem solver for DNA Operations leadership, proactively identifying opportunities and taking ownership of complex or ambiguous challenges that cross traditional functional and organizational boundaries.
* Work with Digital and cross-functional partners to explore how Generative AI and other advanced digital tools can strengthen operational insights, structured problem solving, knowledge access, performance management, and decision making, while operating within appropriate manufacturing, quality, and data-governance requirements.
* Drive success through the team’s ability to execute complex initiatives, deliver sustainable improvements, effectively manage change, enable successful technology transfers, use data proactively to identify opportunities and risks, and continuously strengthen the capability and overall performance of DNA Manufacturing.

**The key Moderna Mindsets you’ll need to succeed in the role:**

* “We act with dynamic range, driving strategy and execution at the same time at every step.”
* “We digitize everywhere possible using the power of code to maximize our impact on patients.”

**Here’s What You’ll Need (Basic Qualifications)**

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, science, manufacturing, or another relevant technical discipline or an equivalent combination of education and relevant industry experience.
* Demonstrated experience in biopharmaceutical manufacturing, technical operations, manufacturing sciences, operational excellence, or a related environment.
* Demonstrated ability to lead and develop people, including creating clarity, setting priorities, coaching performance, and building organizational capability.
* Proven ability to influence and lead effectively within a complex matrix organization, including situations where successful execution requires alignment of stakeholders outside the individual's direct authority.
* Demonstrated ownership and successful execution of complex, cross-functional projects or programs, from problem definition and strategy through implementation and sustained results.
* Experience with GMP manufacturing and quality systems, including change control and other mechanisms used to implement and sustain changes in a regulated environment.
* Experience supporting technology transfer, manufacturing readiness, process implementation, or other cross-functional technical programs.
* Strong understanding of continuous improvement and operational excellence principles, with demonstrated ability to translate them into measurable improvements in manufacturing performance.
* Demonstrated ability to use data, trends, and performance indicators to identify problems, establish priorities, and drive decisions and improvement.
* Strong communication, stakeholder management, and organizational leadership skills, with the ability to communicate effectively from the manufacturing floor through senior leadership.
* Ability to operate effectively in ambiguity, connect technical and business considerations, and take ownership of problems that do not fit neatly within traditional functional boundaries.
* Experience supporting regulatory inspections and inspection readiness activities preferred.

**Schedule:**
Monday–Friday; flexibility may be required to support critical manufacturing activities, technology transfers, regulatory inspections, or significant operational events.
  
  
**Our Working Model**
As we build our company, we have always believed an in-person culture is critical to our success. Moderna champions the significant benefits of in-office collaboration by embracing a 70/30 work model.
  
  
This 70% in-office structure helps to foster a culture rich in innovation, teamwork, and direct mentorship. Join us in shaping a world where every interaction is an opportunity to learn, contribute, and make a meaningful impact.
  
  
Moderna is a smoke-free, alcohol-free, and drug-free work environment.
  
  
**Pay & Benefits**
**At Moderna, we believe that when you feel your best, you can do your best work.**
**That’s why our benefits and well-being resources are designed to support you—at work, at home, and everywhere in between.**

* Competitive healthcare, plus voluntary benefit programs to support your unique needs
* A holistic approach to well-being, with access to fitness, mindfulness, and mental health support
* Family planning benefits, including fertility, adoption, and surrogacy support
* Generous paid time off, including vacation, volunteer days, sabbatical, global recharge days, and a discretionary year-end shutdown
* Savings and investments to help you plan for the future
* Location-specific perks and extras

The salary range for this role is $130,800.00 - $209,400.00. This is the lowest to highest salary we in good faith believe we would pay for this role at the time of this posting. An individual’s position within the salary range will be based on several factors including, but not limited to, specific competencies, relevant education, qualifications, certifications, experience, skills, performance, and business or organizational needs. The successful candidate may be eligible for an annual discretionary bonus, other incentive compensation, or equity award, subject to company plan eligibility criteria and individual performance.
  
  
**About Moderna**
Since our founding in 2010, we have aspired to build the leading mRNA technology platform, the infrastructure to reimagine how medicines are created and delivered, and a world-class team. We believe in giving our people a platform to change medicine and an opportunity to change the world.
  
  
By living our mission, values, and mindsets every day, our people are the driving force behind our scientific progress and our culture. Together, we are creating a culture of belonging and building an organization that cares deeply for our patients, our employees, the environment, and our communities.
  
  
We are proud to have been recognized as a Science Magazine Top Biopharma Employer, a Fast Company Best Workplace for Innovators, and a Great Place to Work in the U.S.
  
  
If you want to make a difference and join a team that is changing the future of medicine, we invite you to visit modernatx.com/careers to learn more about our current opportunities.
  
  
**Equal Opportunities**
Moderna is committed to equal employment opportunity and non-discrimination for all employees and qualified applicants without regard to a person's race, color, sex, gender identity or expression, age, religion, national origin, ancestry or citizenship, ethnicity, disability, military or protected veteran status, genetic information, sexual orientation, marital or familial status, or any other personal characteristic protected under applicable law. Moderna is a place where everyone can grow. If you meet the Basic Qualifications for the role and you would be excited to contribute to our mission every day, please apply!
  
  
Moderna is an E-Verify Employer in the United States. We consider qualified applicants regardless of criminal histories, consistent with legal requirements.
  
  
**Accommodations**
We’re focused on attracting, retaining, developing, and advancing our employees. By cultivating a workplace that values diverse experiences, backgrounds, and ideas, we create an environment where every employee can contribute their best.
  
  
Moderna is committed to offering reasonable accommodations to qualified job applicants with disabilities. Any applicant requiring an accommodation in connection with the hiring process and/or to perform the essential functions of the position for which the applicant has applied should contact the Accommodations team at leavesandaccommodations@modernatx.com.

**About Analog Devices**
Analog Devices, Inc. (NASDAQ: ADI ) is a global semiconductor leader that bridges the physical and digital worlds to enable breakthroughs at the Intelligent Edge. ADI combines analog, digital, and software technologies into solutions that help drive advancements in digitized factories, mobility, and digital healthcare, combat climate change, and reliably connect humans and the world. With revenue of more than $9 billion in FY24 and approximately 24,000 people globally, ADI ensures today's innovators stay Ahead of What's Possible™. Learn more at www.analog.com and on LinkedIn and Twitter (X).
  
  
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
The Camas Wafer Fab is a growing 150mm, high‑volume, 24x7 manufacturing facility producing leading‑edge precision ICs in support of ADI’s diversified semiconductor business.
  
  
Reporting to the Wafer Fab General Manager, the
**Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations**
will lead our ~300‑employee Production organization—including Production Managers, Supervisors, Trainers, 5S & Continuous Improvement, New Product Technicians, Leads, and Operators—who execute day‑to‑day manufacturing, testing, and shipping of a broad product portfolio as the fab continues to ramp, expand, and modernize a facility with over 25 years of operational history.
  
  
Apply now for the opportunity to grow your career and help innovate ahead of what’s possible.
  
  
**Job Duties**
The Senior Manager, Production – Fab Operations is a senior operations leader responsible for translating site strategy into strong operational execution. Responsibilities are aligned to three core competency areas:
  
  
**Operational & Strategic Execution**

* Translate site and enterprise manufacturing strategies into actionable operational plans for the Production organization, aligned with objectives for safety, quality, productivity, cost, talent development, and sustainability.
* Lead the execution of production improvement roadmaps, supporting longer‑term digital transformation, automation, and modernization initiatives defined at the site level.
* Drive adoption of data‑driven and AI‑enabled decision making within production operations, leveraging analytics, automation, and machine‑learning‑based insights to improve daily execution and performance stability.
* Support change management efforts associated with new technologies, digital tools, demand shifts, and new product introductions, ensuring disciplined adoption on the production floor.
* Share and apply best‑known methods from across ADI’s manufacturing network to continuously elevate production performance.

**Operational Excellence**

* Maintain a safe and healthy work environment by enforcing organizational standards, adhering to 5S principles, and complying with ADI policies, legal requirements, and regulatory standards.
* Own day‑to‑day production quality performance, applying a zero‑defect mindset using traditional quality methodologies (8D, 5‑Why, SPC) and AI‑assisted defect detection, yield analysis, and trend identification.
* Lead execution of production plans that deliver short‑term tactical results while driving continuous improvement across Safety, Quality, Productivity, Cost, and Efficiency metrics.
* Utilize predictive and prescriptive analytics, where applicable, to anticipate equipment issues, process drift, capacity constraints, and safety risks before they impact performance.
* Provide clear tactical direction through written reports, dashboards, presentations, daily operational reviews, all‑hands meetings, and shift‑level stand‑ups, ensuring decisions are grounded in accurate, timely data.
* Lead capacity modeling, scenario analysis, and demand response activities within the production organization, partnering with site leadership on longer‑range planning.
* Partner closely with Supply Chain to optimize wafer starts, cycle time, and scheduling, balancing customer demand with fab constraints and operational risk.
* Participate in internal and external audits to ensure compliance, business continuity, and continuous improvement, including adherence to ADI’s responsible and ethical use of AI in manufacturing operations.
* Support the development and ramp of new products and non‑standard fabrication requirements while maintaining safe, stable, and predictable production output.
* Ensure effective cross‑training programs and skills matrices are in place, leveraging digital tools to improve workforce flexibility and readiness.

**Effective Team Leadership**

* Lead recruiting, hiring, onboarding, and training efforts for the Production organization, aligning staffing plans with quarterly and longer‑range production needs.
* Foster a culture of engagement, accountability, and continuous improvement through proactive communication, coaching, and visible leadership presence across all shifts.
* Develop production supervisors and frontline leaders capable of operating in an increasingly digital, automated, and data‑driven manufacturing environment.
* Execute effective performance management processes to improve team continuity, leadership capability, and operational results.
* Partner with Human Resources to support competency development, technical capability building, and training plans aligned with future manufacturing needs.
* Ensure alignment with ADI Enterprise Excellence Guiding Principles, emphasizing safety, quality, operational rigor, and responsible innovation.

**SCHEDULE**
This is an exempt role, working on‑site in Camas, Washington, primarily Monday through Friday, supporting a 24x7 continuous operation.
  
  
Occasional night or weekend hours are required to support operational needs.
  
  
**Minimum Qualifications**

* Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field required; technical or engineering degree strongly preferred.
* 8+ years of leadership experience in high‑volume wafer fabrication or advanced manufacturing operations.
* Demonstrated success leading large production teams through supervisors and frontline leaders.
* Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with proven effectiveness in a data‑driven, metrics‑based operating environment.
* Solid working knowledge of manufacturing and business systems (ERP/MRP, MES, dispatching, capacity planning, Microsoft Office).
* Demonstrated ability to apply analytics, digital tools, and emerging AI/ML capabilities to improve safety, quality, productivity, and cost performance.
* Strong problem‑solving skills, operational discipline, and passion for continuous improvement.

*For positions requiring access to technical data, Analog Devices, Inc. may have to obtain export licensing approval from the U.S. Department of Commerce - Bureau of Industry and Security and/or the U.S. Department of State - Directorate of Defense Trade Controls. As such, applicants for this position – except US Citizens, US Permanent Residents, and protected individuals as defined by 8 U.S.C. 1324b(a)(3) – may have to go through an export licensing review process.*
*Analog Devices is an equal opportunity employer. We foster a culture where everyone has an opportunity to succeed regardless of their race, color, religion, age, ancestry, national origin, social or ethnic origin, sex, sexual orientation, gender, gender identity, gender expression, marital status, pregnancy, parental status, disability, medical condition, genetic information, military or veteran status, union membership, and political affiliation, or any other legally protected group.*

Job Req Type: Experienced
  
  
Required Travel: No
  
  
Shift Type: 1st Shift/Days
  
  
The expected wage range for a new hire into this position is $143,200 to $196,900.
  
  

* Actual wage offered may vary depending on work location, experience, education, training, external market data, internal pay equity, or other bona fide factors.
* This position qualifies for a discretionary performance-based bonus which is based on personal and company factors
* This position includes medical, vision and dental coverage, 401k, paid vacation, holidays, and sick time, and other benefits.
